data.summary:
R2 CRITIQUE of Greenfield-Senior slice S2 (ownership map, path-scoped permissions, slice closure)
Reviewer role: security-reviewer. Independent, no prior context. Work done in a clone at review-r2/copy;
reproductions in review-r2/repro. Baseline S2 suites (gf-close, gf-own, gf-permissions) run green on the tree
under review: 234 tests, 0 fail. (A machine-wide disk-full occurred ~16:25-16:35Z; every reproduction below was
re-run afterward with >4 GB free and is not a disk artifact.)

WHAT I ATTACKED
The slice claims, in sections 16 and 17: path-scoped ownership (GF-OWN-1..5), contract-path writes to api only
(GF-FRZ-1), guard-config pinning (GF-CONF-1), the L-GF-17 spoof assessment and preflight, and the three-step
adversarial slice-closure rule (GF-CLOSE-1..5) that is the mechanism used to close S2 itself. I went after the
closure rule hardest, because a hole there means a slice can be declared closed without the protection the owner
asked for ("every finding reproduced as a failing test before any fix", two real batteries, independent review).
I forged events through Store.commit (B1), reused and relabelled evidence, and drove the managed path
(closure.recordReview / resolveFinding / runBattery / close) directly.

WHAT BROKE (two findings; reproductions named in findings.json)
1. BLOCKING - GF-CLOSE-2 does not bind a fix-verify proof to the finding it resolves. closure.js
   resolutionProblems/closeProblems check only that a cited proof is a well-formed fix-verify pair recorded after
   the finding; nothing checks the proof belongs to that finding or is used once. On the fully managed path, one
   real fix-verify pair "resolves: fixed" any number of distinct findings. I closed a slice carrying two (and
   three) BLOCKING critique findings where only one fix ever happened; gf audit is clean. This defeats owner
   condition 1 and GF-CLOSE-2 on the path where it is claimed. Repro: repro/r2-close2.test.js.
2. MAJOR - GF-CLOSE-3 counts battery events, not distinct runs, and never binds a battery's evidence to its tree.
   closure.js batteryProblems only checks the cited evidence is some recorded mutation run; closeProblems counts
   gf.battery.recorded events and reads treeHash/survivors from the event. A forged second battery that re-cites
   round 1's evidence, or that relabels a pre-fix run's evidence with the closing tree, satisfies "two batteries,
   the last on the closing tree" and closes; a survivor hidden by an empty event list needs no reason. gf audit
   reports clean, although section 8 says a B1-forged gf.* event "must be caught by gf audit", and 16.5 lists
   exactly these ("one battery only", "a second battery on the pre-fix tree") as bypasses that must fail.
   Repro: repro/r2-battery.test.js.

WHAT HELD
Ownership resisted every route I tried. The real PreToolUse hook denies a group role writing another group's
path through Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit and through shell redirect/tee/sed -i/cp/mv/truncate, judges the
normalised path (app/../web/x.js), follows symlinked directories (resolveReal), and fails closed when the sealed
breakdown.json is tampered (GF-OWN-1). GF-FRZ-1 keeps sealed contract files to the api group and only while an
amendment request is open. A forged gf.ownership.amended by a non-reviewer, a stale-chain amendment, and a forged
task.completed listing a foreign file are all caught by gf audit (GF-OWN-5/GF-OWN-3). GF-CONF-1 pin drift is
detected. The closure rule held against the obvious attacks: a review bound to an earlier tree, a reviewer that is
the closer or that authored work, a non-reviewer actor, a review on a dirty tree, malformed/blank accounting, a
dispatch whose inputs name the implementers' working record, a double close, and any review/resolution/battery
for an already-closed scope are all refused or flagged. L-GF-17 (actor asserted, not bound) is stated honestly and
its residual is an admitted limit; preflight reports the regime from the installed settings.json truthfully. The
proof-to-finding gap (1) and the battery-evidence gap (2) are the two places the closure guarantee is weaker than
the design states.

findings.summary: GF-CLOSE-2 never binds a fix-verify proof to the finding it resolves. closure.js resolutionProblems (lib/greenfield/closure.js:188-245) only checks a cited proof is a well-formed fix-verify pair recorded after the finding, and closeProblems (lib/greenfield/closure.js:325-329) only checks each finding has some resolution; neither checks the proof is that finding's or is used once. On the managed path one real fix-verify pair resolves any number of distinct BLOCKING critique findings, so a slice closes with findings that were never individually reproduced or fixed (defeats owner condition 1 and GF-CLOSE-2 where it is claimed); gf audit reports clean. Reproduction: review-r2/repro/r2-close2.test.js (both subtests pass: a slice with two/three blocking findings closes citing one shared proof).

GF-CLOSE-3 counts battery EVENTS and never binds a battery's evidence to its treeHash or to a unique run. closure.js batteryProblems (lib/greenfield/closure.js:259-272) checks only that the cited evidence is some recorded mutation run; closeProblems (lib/greenfield/closure.js:330-343) counts gf.battery.recorded events and reads treeHash/survivors from the event, not the evidence. A B1-forged second battery that re-cites round 1's evidence, or that relabels a pre-fix run's evidence with the closing tree, satisfies 'two batteries, the last on the closing tree after the last fix' and closes; a real survivor is hidden with an empty survivors list and needs no accepted reason. gf audit reports clean although section 8 says a B1-forged gf.* event must be caught by gf audit and 16.5 lists exactly these as bypasses that must fail. Reproduction: review-r2/repro/r2-battery.test.js (three subtests pass: reused evidence, pre-fix-tree relabel, hidden survivor).

Plan vs design 16.2/17.2: the plan builds 'the slice-closure rule GF-CLOSE-1..4' (Goal, Task 5 title, T7 Step 1 battery list). Task 5's interfaces have no gf.dispatch.recorded and no GF-CLOSE-5. Its gf.review.recorded is '{id, scope, treeHash, verdict: clean|findings, findings: [{id, severity, summary}]}', with no step, dispatch, summary, finding kind (documentation/defect), readiness go/no-go or ev:/path:line citations. Its gf.slice.closed cites a single 'review'. The plan's Spec line cites sections 16, 4.2 and 8, not 17. The only amendment note (Task 7) covers process, and T7 Steps 3-4 still say 'a fresh general-purpose agent, given the code, the design section 16 and this plan' and 'review pass 2 (a fresh agent)', which contradicts 17.2 (R1 from documents alone, three dispatches). Built from the plan, the closure rule would be the pre-17.2 one.

17.2 'What the engine enforces (GF-CLOSE-1 and GF-CLOSE-5, with GF-CLOSE-2 to 4 as in section 16.5)': GF-CLOSE-5 is named but its condition is never separated from the amended GF-CLOSE-1. One sentence lists dispatch-before-review, refused inputs, review cites dispatch, one review per dispatch, reviewer authored nothing, a review of each step, readiness go. The table in 16.5 still has rows GF-CLOSE-1 to 4 only. GF-CLOSE-5 has no bypass list, although section 8 requires positive, negative and bypass tests per rule. gf.dispatch.recorded's fields are given only in prose ('naming the reviewer role, the step, the tree ... and the input artifacts with their hashes'). Which rule id reports which violation cannot be reconstructed.

The closing-round condition is contradictory. 16.5 GF-CLOSE-1 says 'the latest review of the scope has verdict: clean', and 16.8 step 4 says 'Review round 2 on the final tree ... clean and readiness go'. But 17.2 says 'the closing tree needs a review of each step, the readiness verdict go, no unresolved finding', which admits resolved findings, and 17.9 P7 predicts 'the closing round ... will raise at least one finding'. Not stated: whether closing-round R1/R2 must have zero findings; what happens when round 2 raises a finding (17.2 and the '5 to 6 reviewer dispatches' of 17.9 assume exactly two rounds); how a 'fixed' finding, which changes HEAD^{tree} (a documentation fix included), can coexist with reviews bound to the closing tree; which verdict values R1 and R2 carry (plan: clean|findings; R3: go|no-go).

How S2 itself is closed is contradictory. 16.5 says 'The process in 16.8 follows the rule by hand and records each element in the evidence file: the ECCode build is not a Greenfield-Senior project, so the engine cannot yet run it on its own slices'. 16.8 step 4 (and plan T7's amendment line) says 'S2's closure is recorded in a Greenfield-Senior record kept beside a checkout of the final tree, by the closure rule itself', under the heading 'the closure rule applied to S2 by hand'. Not explained: how GF-CLOSE-1's 'bound to the git tree object (HEAD^{tree}) ... on a clean tracked tree' binds to a checkout when the record lives 'beside' it. Also unstated: in a fresh record with no claim, completion or gate submission, the 'authored nothing in the record' condition holds trivially and so shows nothing for S2.

'Battery' has three meanings that are never reconciled: (1) section 8's 'generic bypass battery' B1-B5; (2) 16.5 GF-CLOSE-3's 'pinned mutation runs: tree clean before and after, evidence recorded by the engine', with plan T5 'closure.runBattery(..., {scope, test, base, max}) (calls the frozen mutate.run ...)', where test, base and max are undefined; (3) plan T7 Step 1's 'scratchpad/mutation-run.js extended with GF-OWN-1 ... Expected: every rule fails at least two tests when removed', a rule-removal script outside the tree. 16.1(1)(c) adds 'a second mutation or battery run'. Not stated: which of these satisfies GF-CLOSE-3 for S2; whether a scratchpad script can produce 'evidence recorded by the engine'; whether a kill threshold applies; the basis for 'at least two tests'.

Is GF-OWN-3 keyed on the actor or on the path? 16.2 says 'every listed changed file belongs to the completing actor's group', and plan T3 has 'completionProblems(map, actor, filesChanged)'. But 16.4 F1 says 'GF-OWN-3 and GF-OWN-4 judge paths against the sealed map, not actor strings, so a spoofed actor buys less'. For a forged task.completed by actor B, on a task owned by A, listing B's files, the two readings give opposite audit results. F1 also says 'sealed map' where 16.2/16.3 and GF-OWN-3 use the effective (amended) map 'in force at that event'.

Pre-seal behaviour of group roles is contradictory, and gate authors that are group roles are not addressed. Plan Review Focus 4 says 'A group role called while the project is not yet sealed ...: the hook fails closed with the reason (GF-OWN-1 hash mismatch)'. Plan T2's positive row says 'pre-seal group roles hold no claims, so this row asserts the existing "no claimed task" message is still what a pre-seal write gets' (the sentence itself is truncated: 'before the seal...'). Design 16.2 states neither behaviour. delivery-lead is a group role (2.4; plan T2 'delivery-lead and devops-engineer are group delivery') and authors plan.json, breakdown.json and estimates.json (3.1 stages 5-6), which must exist before the seal. GF-OWN-2 ('inside its group's globs and a claimed task's globs') and T2's bypass 'a delivery-lead write outside Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, Makefile, docs/**' would deny those writes. No document says where the G1 artifacts live or how a gate author that is a group role writes them.

GF-FRZ-1 is underspecified. (a) 3.4 point 1 'writable only by integration-engineer' and 16.2 'writable by the api group only' conflict with 3.1 stage 3, where technical-designer authors the contracts before the seal, unless the rule binds group roles only. The design never says so; only plan T2 implies it ('null means ... role is in no group'). (b) 'only while an amendment request for that file is open': 'open' is undefined. Is a request closed by gf.contract.amended? Section 7 has no rejection or withdrawal event. (c) 16.2 lists GF-FRZ-1 'At: H, A', but file writes are not log events, no document says what the audit half checks, and plan T2 tests only the hook. (d) Not stated whether mocks/** (api-reserved in 16.3) and contracts/ux-spec.json count as 'contract paths'.

GF-CONF-1 re-pin semantics are not stated. Plan T4 lets the orchestrator or user pin at any time with a reason of 10 or more characters; 'a second pin moves the expected hashes'; drift 'compares the latest pin with the bytes now', although each pin carries a 'scope'. Not stated: whether a re-pin within a scope or slice is allowed; whether 'latest' is per scope; whether creating a config file that was absent at pin time counts as drift. So 4.1's 'An agent cannot weaken the security policy by editing them' and section 8's bypass 'loosen a security.json cell mid-slice' hold only against group roles. A loosened file re-pinned by the orchestrator is accepted, and no limit says so. Also, plan T2 attributes the group-role denial on .eccode/behavior.json to the 'record rule, unchanged', while T4 attributes it to GF-CONF-1. And 4.1's gf.slice.opened configHashes is not reconciled with gf.config.pinned.

The accounting unit for delegated agents is not stated. 16.1(2) fixes 'The unit is all processed tokens (input + output + cache reads + cache writes)' for 'one ledger row per slice and per delegated agent'. But 16.6 takes a delegated agent's figure from 'subagent_tokens' in its completion notice, without saying whether that figure includes cache reads and writes. So 16.7's '0.3 to 0.6 M tokens each as reported (S1's: 419,658)' and 17.9's '0.3 to 0.8 M tokens as reported' are in an unstated unit, possibly not the owner's. Also not stated: that GF-CLOSE-4 checks only the form of start/end (the numbers are the closer's assertion), and how to record a session restart that resets the cumulative counter (end < start, which is refused).

Who may close, and what counts as authoring, are not stated. GF-CLOSE-1 requires the reviewer 'is not the closer', but no document says which roles may commit gf.slice.closed ('eccode-gf close', plan 'close seal', 'gf_close'). 'authored nothing in the record (no claim, completion or gate submission under that role)' does not say whether contract or ownership amendments, finding resolutions, pins or messages count as authoring. GF-CLOSE-2's 'withdrawn only by a reviewer role' does not say whether that may be the finding's own reviewer or must meet the independence condition. 'deferred ... with a limit id' does not say what the id is checked against.

The fix proof for documentation findings is undefined. 16.5 says 'A documentation finding ... is proven by a paired run of one command (failed as a reproduction, then passed)', but does not say what command can reproduce a documentation defect (an undefined term, a contradiction), or how it is recorded as evidence with 'purpose: reproduction'. Nor does it reconcile this with owner decision 16.1(1)(b), 'every finding reproduced as a failing test before any fix'. For code findings, plan T5 requires only that the post-fix evidence carries fixVerify.preFix; whether the pre-fix and post-fix runs must be the same command is not stated. 'fix-verify', 'fixVerify.preFix' and 'purpose: reproduction' are used without definition.

The documents disagree on which map version each rule applies. GF-OWN-3 uses 'the map in force at that event'. GF-OWN-1 in plan T1 uses 'files inside the group at the seal or the last rescope', while 16.2 says 'effective globs'. GF-OWN-4's 'attribution({map, tasks, changed})' does not say which map. 16.3 refuses an amendment that strands a pending or claimed task but allows one that strands a completed task, after which GF-OWN-1, -3 and -4 can disagree. Also, 16.2 says 'gf.g1.sealed.hashes' where plan T1 says 'gf.seal.hashes'.

16.3 is titled 'Effective map and its algebra' but gives only the replacement chain. It does not describe how disjointness of glob sets with ** and denyGlobs is decided (plan T1: 'a to that overlaps another group without deny'). Nor does it say whether an amendment can change denyGlobs; the event carries only from/to globs (plan T1).

Drafts and other .eccode paths. 16.2 says 'group roles write only .eccode/drafts/<group>/**', yet L-GF-4 still says '.eccode/drafts/** stays a shared scratch area', without saying in what sense: reads are not intercepted (C6), and non-group roles are unrestricted. GF-OWN-2's 'a path owned by no group is refused' does not say whether other .eccode/ paths a group role must write are exempt (for example the handoffs used at completion, plan T3). Plan T3 ignores .eccode/ paths only for completionProblems, not for the hook.

Clean-tree definition and post-close commits. Design GF-CLOSE-1 says 'on a clean tracked tree'; plan T5 says 'git status --porcelain is empty outside .eccode/'. Porcelain also lists untracked files, and excluding .eccode/ lets uncommitted edits to the tracked guard configs under .eccode/ pass. Not stated: whether a closure stays valid after the tree moves (16.8: 'no commit after it other than evidence'; compare section 5, where DONE is a projection invalidated by any later change), or how 'other than evidence' is checked.

Section 7 'Event reference' is not updated for S2. It lacks gf.config.pinned, gf.review.recorded, gf.finding.resolved, gf.battery.recorded, gf.slice.closed and gf.dispatch.recorded. It still lists gf.ownership.amended as '{id, group, globs, reason}', whereas 16.3 and plan T1 use from/to/message. Neither section 7 nor 17.2 gives the verdict values per review step.

16.4 F0: the preflight reports, 'as a recorded fact and not an assumption, which regime is in force'. Plan T6 returns a value and an audit warning, and no event is defined, so it is unclear whether 'recorded' means a log event. The regime is read from the current settings, so it says nothing about the regime when past events were committed. That fits L-GF-17's 'cannot see a failure afterwards' but not the wording 'recorded fact'. The handling of the 'unknown' profile (no warning stated) is also not given.

16.8 step 1 says 'the Mealie and kotlinc skips remain and are named' but omits the ECCODE_CBM skip and codebase-memory-mcp, both listed in section 13 ('1 needs ECCODE_CBM; 2 need kotlinc / codebase-memory-mcp'). It also does not state the expected skip count after the change (49 before minus the 35 FastAPI tests).

Several estimate figures have a basis that does not reproduce or is missing. (1) 17.7: 'wall times are the registered figures of section 10 scaled by the measured S1 ratio (about one fifth)'. But S1's 1 h 22 min against 8-14 h is about 1/6 to 1/10, and S3/S5/S6 (1.5-3, 1.5-3, 1-2 h) exceed one fifth of 6-10, 4-7 and 2-3 h; the allowance for review rounds is not quantified. (2) 16.6's Cost column ($5.74, $24.70, $18.96) has no stated source, while D6 and section 10 say 'Dollar figures are not given'. (3) 16.7's 'Tests ... table rows now counted' does not define the unit to be scored. (4) 17.9 says '5 to 6 reviewer dispatches', but the rounds it lists make 5.

Limit numbering is inconsistent. Section 15 says S1's limits are 'L-GF-1 to L-GF-16', yet 15.1 names L-GF-18 for S1 (m4), and the register lists L-GF-17 ('S1, restated S2') and L-GF-18 ('S1'). Section 11's table stops at L-GF-13 and its heading still says 'Limits to register in docs/limits.md'.

There is no as-built record for S2. Plan T7 lists 'docs/design/greenfield-senior.md (section 17 as built)', but section 17 is the owner-continuation registration, and sections 16 and 17 are headed 'design ... written before any S2 code'. Yet 16.2 has a column 'Built in S2 as' and 17.1 says 'built and used to close S2'. There is no S2 counterpart to section 15 ('S1 as built', with its deviations), so from these documents a reader cannot tell whether S2 deviated from 16/17 or how P4-P7 came out.

17.4 GF-UX-1 says 'every screen has all four states and a test id for each; denied is required for every screen whose operations have a deny cell'. If all four states are always required, the second clause is vacuous. 17.4 also says 'S4a adds that reserved path [contracts/ux-spec.json] to GF-WBS-2', but contracts/** is already reserved to api (16.3).

17.5 and 17.8 #7 say 'hash the raw output in memory, persist the redacted output, record both hashes'. But T2 says 'the engine only ever runs it with --redact and no raw report exists to persist'. For Gitleaks there is no unredacted output to hash, so what rawSha256 means for T2 is undefined.

17.2 refuses 'inputs under the implementers' working record (drafts, handoffs, memory, runs, lab, the event log)' by category, never by path. 16.8 step 3 says reviewers get 'the artifacts and the tree, not my conclusions', but the tree every reviewer receives contains the implementer's conclusions: for example 16.4 'Finding', 16.6's lesson, and the evidence file named in 16.8. This residual is not stated as a limit next to L-GF-19.

3.4 point 2, 'Completion (P): a task whose files include contract paths is refused unless it belongs to the api group and cites an amendment', has no rule id. 16.2 does not assign it to S2 or any later slice. GF-OWN-3 covers group membership but not 'cites an amendment', and how a task cites an amendment is not defined.

data.summary:
What S2 builds and why. After the G1 seal, S2 makes group ownership binding. The map is the groups section of the sealed breakdown.json (name, role, globs, denyGlobs), and every read re-hashes that file against the seal. A mismatch is a GF-OWN-1 problem, and the hook then denies all group-role writes (fail closed). The map changes only through gf.ownership.amended: a reviewer role, a reason of at least 30 characters, a cited message, and a `from` equal to the globs in force (a chain). Each amendment's `to` replaces that group's globs, in log order. Every map must pass the breakdown checks: groups disjoint after denyGlobs; contracts/** and mocks/** belong to api; tests/acceptance/** belongs to test. An amendment may not strand a pending or claimed task. Any overlap the glob algebra cannot prove is a denied sub-tree is refused.

Enforcement. GF-OWN-1: the seal half is GF-WBS-1/2, and the audit checks the engine's tasks against the map. GF-OWN-2 (hook): a group role's write must lie inside its group's globs and inside a claimed task's globs. An unowned path is refused, and drafts go only under .eccode/drafts/<group>/. Before the seal, the existing claimed-task rule decides. GF-OWN-3 wraps task_complete: the listed files must belong to the actor's group, and (16.4 F1, section 18) the actor must own the task. The audit replays each completion against the map in force at that event. GF-OWN-4 (eccode-gf attribute --base) checks that every changed path was declared by a completed task of the owning group; it joins the audit in S4. GF-OWN-5 also wraps rescope, so a task cannot leave its group. GF-FRZ-1: only the api group writes contract files, and after the seal only while an amendment request for that file is open.

Guard-config pin (GF-CONF-1). gf.config.pinned hashes whichever of behavior.json, guards.json and security.json exist. Only the orchestrator or the user pins, and either may re-pin at any time with a reason. The latest pin is the reference. Any change, deletion or new file after it is drift, which the audit reports, and the hook refuses group-role writes to these files. A loosened file that is re-pinned is visible, not refused (L-GF-22).

Closure (GF-CLOSE-1 to 5). The orchestrator or the user runs eccode-gf close, which commits gf.slice.closed after an in-lock check that the audit replays. The check needs a clean closing tree (HEAD^{tree}, ignoring .eccode/) and a review of each step on it: R1 comprehension (documentation findings), R2 critique (defects) and R3 readiness (go or no-go, citing ev:<id> or path:line). The reviewer is a configured reviewer role that authored nothing (no claim, completion or gate submission) and is not the closer. Each review cites its own earlier gf.dispatch.recorded (role, step, tree, hashed inputs, working-record paths refused, one review per dispatch). Every finding is resolved: fixed with a fix-verify proof (a paired run for documentation), withdrawn by a reviewer with a reason, or deferred by the user (minor only, with a limit id). There must be two or more engine mutation batteries: the first before the first review, the last on the closing tree after the last fix, survivors with reasons. Accounting is {all-processed-tokens, start, end}, each an integer or "unmeasurable". After closure nothing more is recorded for the scope. S2 closes itself this way, in a fresh record.

Identity. The log asserts an actor but does not bind it. Section 16.4 concludes that ownership is spoofable on the managed path in the sense that matters: it holds only while the per-role server lock (with the harness tool list) and the hook are in force, and a failure of either is invisible afterwards. Built: a preflight reporting the current regime (not a log event), rules relying on plan facts (the task's owner), and a restated L-GF-17. Keyed attestation (L-GF-20) is proposed for S5.

Accounting. The unit is input + output + cache-read + cache-write tokens, cumulative from the harness, snapshotted at slice start and end. Delegated agents are recorded "as reported"; an unknown cell says "unmeasurable". GF-CLOSE-4 checks form, not truth.

Not guaranteed: actor binding (L-GF-17); reviewer zero context, only attested (L-GF-19); authors' views in the tree (L-GF-23); draft reads (L-GF-4); sub-agent identity (L-GF-3); re-pins (L-GF-22); write checks with hooks off; commits after closure.

findings.summary: 16.5 / 16.8 / 17.2 / plan T5, T7: the closing-round verdict contradicts itself. The GF-CLOSE-1 row requires 'the latest review of the scope has verdict: clean'. 16.8 step 4 and plan Task 7 step 4 say 'clean and readiness go', and plan Task 5 lists 'verdict findings (GF-CLOSE-1)' as a refusal. But 16.5 'The closing round, stated once' and 17.2 ask only for 'a review of each step', readiness go and every finding resolved, and add 'A finding withdrawn or deferred leaves the tree as it is', so a closing round may carry findings. The amendment note ("the latest review" below reads "a review of each step on the closing tree, readiness go") does not say whether the verdict-clean clause still applies. A reader cannot tell whether a closing-round comprehension or critique review with verdict findings, all withdrawn or deferred, allows closure.

16.5 Definitions / plan T5 as-built: the conditions of the paired-run proof are not stated. The design says only 'one command ... recorded with eccode evidence run --purpose reproduction while it fails, then recorded again after the fix while it passes', and the plan adds 'proof, reproduction? (a paired run for documentation findings)'. Missing: (1) how the engine checks that the two runs are 'one command' (fix-verify links them through fixVerify.preFix; no link is named for a paired run); (2) whether both runs must fall after the finding and before the resolution (GF-CLOSE-2 states this only for fix-verify); (3) whether the reproduction must fail with an assertion; (4) whether a paired run is accepted only for kind documentation, and whether kind is tied to the review step. Without (4), a defect finding could be marked fixed with the weaker proof.

16.5 'How S2 itself is closed' / 16.8 / plan T7 / 17.1: S2's own closure cannot be reconstructed. 16.5 says the record 'is initialised inside a separate checkout of the final tree' and 'The record is new'. 16.8 step 4 and the plan say it is 'kept beside' a checkout of the final tree. 16.8 is headed 'the closure rule applied to S2 by hand', but its step 4 says 'by the closure rule itself'. No document says whether round 1 (R1 and R2 on the build tree), its findings, their fix-verify proofs and battery 1 are recorded in that fresh record. If they are not, GF-CLOSE-2's proof ordering and GF-CLOSE-3's 'first recorded before the first review ... last ... recorded after the last fixed resolution' are met vacuously in S2's own closure. 17.1's 'built and used to close S2' then cannot be checked from these documents; they point to gf-s2-evidence.md.

Plan Task 7 step 1 vs 16.5: the plan names the wrong battery as battery 1. Step 1 reads 'Battery run 1 on the build tree: scratchpad/mutation-run.js extended with GF-OWN-1, ... Expected: every rule fails at least two tests when removed'. That is the rule-removal battery, which 16.5 item (3) says 'does not satisfy GF-CLOSE-3'; only step 4 names 'the engine's battery run 2'. Following the plan gives one engine battery, and GF-CLOSE-3 requires 'at least two batteries (pinned mutation runs ...)'. 16.8 step 3 'Battery run 1 on the build tree' does not say which kind. Section 18 mentions 'the first engine battery' without saying when or on which tree it ran.

16.4 'What a spoof does not buy' and L-GF-17 overstate a guarantee. They say the sealed contracts, the pinned guard configs and the sealed acceptance tests 'are content-addressed ...: any change to them is detected whoever made it'. Yet 16.4 also concedes that A can act as a reviewer ('an A agent acting as a reviewer could amend the map'). Each of these artifacts has a legitimate change path that a spoofed actor can use: gf.contract.amended (3.4, reviewer only), gf.acceptance.amended (4.6, reviewer) and an orchestrator re-pin, which L-GF-22 says is 'accepted with a reason ... not refused'. A change made through these paths by a spoofed reviewer or orchestrator is recorded but not flagged. The claim is stated without that qualification.

Register header, L-GF-1 and the plan's 'Enforcement wording': 'prevention on the managed (MCP) path plus guaranteed detection by log-replay audit in all profiles'. In S2 that wording does not hold for cross-group file writes. GF-OWN-2 is 'H' only (16.2); file writes are not log events; GF-OWN-3 judges only the files a completion lists; and GF-OWN-4 is 'a pure function and a command; its audit integration waits for S4'. So with hooks off (16.4 last row; plan Task 2 'with ECCODE_HOOKS=off the hook allows'), a write into another group's files that no completion lists is not detected by the audit. It is found only if someone runs eccode-gf attribute. No limit in the register states this S2 residual, and the headline wording contradicts it.

16.5: two statements give different rules for who may withdraw a finding. The GF-CLOSE-2 row says 'withdrawn only by a reviewer role, with a reason' (any reviewer role). The 'Who closes' paragraph says 'A finding is withdrawn only by the reviewer role that raised it'. Plan Task 5's tests ('withdrawn by the orchestrator') do not settle which one the engine enforces.

16.2: the audit half of GF-FRZ-1 is never stated. The table gives GF-FRZ-1 'At: H, A' (section 8 says 'H,P,A'), but no text says what the audit checks for it. The clarifications call GF-FRZ-2 'the audit half of the contract rules' and give 3.4 point 2's completion check to 'GF-OWN-3 and GF-FRZ-1'. The documents do not say what the audit condition is or whether GF-FRZ-1 has a P point.

16.2 / 16.4 / 18 / plan T3: GF-OWN-3 is stated three ways. The 16.2 table defines it as 'every listed changed file belongs to the completing actor's group'. 16.4 F1 (headed 'assessment, before building') adds 'the actor must be the task's owner'. Section 18 records that addition as a deviation from review round 1 (R1-6). Plan Task 3's interface completionProblems(map, actor, filesChanged) has no input for the task's owner, and Task 3 has no as-built block. The full rule can be recovered from 16.4 and 18, but the table and the plan still state the narrower one.

16.3 vs plan Task 1 step 3: the GF-OWN-1 audit is defined two ways. The 16.3 table judges it against 'the effective map now, for pending and claimed tasks'. The plan has the audit check 'every engine task (owner in a group, files inside the group at the seal or the last rescope)'. They disagree on which tasks (all, or pending and claimed) and on which map (now, or at the seal or last rescope).

3.2 / plan T1 / plan T2: three sources for a role's group. The 3.2 breakdown schema has groups {name, role, globs[], denyGlobs[]}, one role per group. Plan Task 1 has mapOf -> {groups: {[name]: {roles, globs, denyGlobs}}}, with several roles. Plan Task 2 says 'Role to group through C.groupOf; delivery-lead and devops-engineer are group delivery', which is a constant. The documents do not say whether the sealed breakdown or the constant decides a role's group, or what happens when they disagree; 16.3 says only that 'an amendment cannot change ... roles'.

16.5 GF-CLOSE-1 'recorded by a configured reviewer role'; section 7 '"reviewer" means a configured reviewer role'; plan Task 1 'reviewersOf(config)'. No document says which configuration keys define the reviewer set (the reviewers of every gate, or of one gate), although GF-OWN-5, GF-CLOSE-1 and GF-CLOSE-2 all depend on it.

Section 7 vs plan Task 5: the documents disagree on where a survivor's reason is recorded. Section 7 gives gf.battery.recorded 'survivors[{key}]' and gf.slice.closed 'accepted[{key, reason}]'. Plan Task 5 also puts 'survivors: [{key, reason}]' in the battery event. GF-CLOSE-3 says 'its survivors listed with a reason each', and 16.5 says 'every survivor of the last battery needs an accepted reason'. The battery event, the close event, or both: the documents do not agree.

16.5 GF-CLOSE-4: a bypass the rule cannot detect. The bypass column says ''0' standing for unknown' must fail, but the same row accepts any non-negative integer, so a numeric 0 cannot be told apart from a measured 0. Plan Task 5 tests ''0' as a string' instead. The design does not say which it means.

16.5 GF-CLOSE-5 and 17.2 require that 'the orchestrator records a dispatch (gf.dispatch.recorded) before each review', but neither document names how. Plan Task 5 lists the CLI 'eccode-gf close review|resolve|battery|seal' and the MCP tools gf_review_record, gf_finding_resolve, gf_battery_run and gf_close, with no command, tool or function for a dispatch. Also unstated: whether the input hashes are checked against the files in the dispatch's tree; 17.2 says only 'checked for form'.

17.2 R3: 'cites evidence: an executed check (ev:<id>) or path:line in the tree, each resolved by the engine'. The documents do not say whether a readiness review must cite at least one item, or what 'resolved' means for a path:line citation (the file exists in the closing tree? the line exists?).

16.5 GF-CLOSE-2 / section 7: no rule says who may mark a finding fixed. GF-CLOSE-2 says who may withdraw (a reviewer role) and who may defer (the user), and section 7 gives gf.finding.resolved 'Who: see GF-CLOSE-2', but no document says which roles may record a 'fixed' resolution.

Section 7 / plan Task 5 vs GF-CLOSE-2: gf.finding.resolved names a finding only by 'finding', while GF-CLOSE-2 resolves 'every finding of every review of the scope'. The documents do not say whether finding ids must be unique across all reviews of a scope, or how a resolution picks out a finding of one particular review. Section 18 cites round-1 ids such as 'R1-6' and 'R2-1'.

Section 11 says the register 'is authoritative' and 'later limits are added to the register only', but several S2 residuals named in the design are missing from docs/limits-greenfield.md: (1) an amendment request with 'no withdrawal event ... keeps its file writable for the api group' (16.2); (2) a deferral limit id 'that the engine does not check against the register (a named residual)' (16.5); (3) 'no commit after it other than evidence is my discipline, not an engine check' (16.5); (4) 'GF-CLOSE-4 checks the form of the numbers, not their truth' (16.6); (5) the battery has 'no kill threshold', and nothing constrains --test, --base or --max (16.5). Separately, 16.2 says the 'cites an amendment' half of 3.4 point 2 'is registered for S4b', but neither S4b's scope in 17.7 nor the register lists it.

18, Preflight row: 'As designed: "a recorded fact"'. That wording appears nowhere else in the design, and 16.4 F0 already says the preflight is 'computed from the current settings each time; it is not a log event'. The deviation row cites a design statement a reader cannot find.

16.7, wall-time basis: 'S2 has about 1.5 times the scope' (of S1, by an unstated measure). The same table registers 900 to 1,500 production lines, against S1's 2.3 k (17.7), which is 0.4 to 0.65 times. The measure behind the factor of 1.5 is not stated.

17.7 basis: 'the ranges above are the registered figures of section 10 scaled by factors of about one quarter to two thirds (S3 0.25 to 0.3, S5 about 0.4, S6 0.5 to 0.67)'. S4a and S4b have no stated factor or basis, and their build time together (5 to 10 h) against section 10's S4 build (6 to 10 h) is a factor of about 0.8 to 1.0, outside the stated range.

17.5 vs 17.8 item 7: the two contradict each other for the secret scanner. 17.5 says 'for Gitleaks, rawSha256 is the hash of the redacted report, because the engine never produces an unredacted one'. 17.8 item 7 says, for the secret scanner, 'hash the raw output in memory, persist the redacted output, record both hashes'.

17.3 GF-PRE-2 (registered for S4a): every resolution 'binds to an artifact that exists at the seal: ... a test id', with test binds checked at the seal (also 17.8 item 1). Acceptance tests are written after the seal (4.6; GF-ORD-1, 'nothing is claimed ... before the seal'), so 'test id' is either undefined (a test task? a test file?) or cannot exist at the seal. Also, GF-PRE-2's 'At' column reads 'seal ..., audit', while 17.8 item 1 adds a check at design-gate submission.

17.3 GF-PRE-3 (registered for S4b): 'slice integration refuses unless every task.failed, task.rescoped, contract amendment request and blocker message ... cites an anticipated entry or a discovered record'. task.failed and task.rescoped are frozen-engine events and carry no GF citation. gf.problem.discovered's 'cause' points the other way, and no field links an engine event to an anticipated register entry. The documents do not say how the citation is made.

16.2 clarifications: 'the contract files are the five sealed files plus contracts/events.json'. 3.1 lists contracts/events.json as an optional contract, and 3.4 seals 'every contract file'. The documents do not say whether events.json is sealed when present, and therefore whether the api group needs an open amendment request to write it after the seal.

Plan Task 2: the policy() interface contradicts the pre-seal rule. It says policy 'Fails closed: if the map cannot be loaded the denial says why' and 'a denial wins'. Before the seal no map can be loaded, yet the 16.2 clarifications, Review Focus 4 and the Task 2 test row say a pre-seal write gets 'the existing "no claimed task" message'. The interface does not say that policy returns no denial before the seal. That test row is also listed under 'positive:' although it asserts a denial.

data.summary:
R2 critique of S2 (security-reviewer), on a clone of the dispatched tree (HEAD 010ac02). Inputs read: docs/design/greenfield-senior.md sections 2, 15 to 18, the S2 plan, docs/limits-greenfield.md, and the code in lib/greenfield (ownership, ownership-ops, permissions, pin, closure, audit, events, projection, preflight, wrap, index), scripts/hooks/guard.js, lib/mcp.js, the frozen tasks, store, fixverify and mutate functions S2 calls, and the gf tests and fixtures. Each finding below has a script in review-c2/ that runs against the clone. I ran each one and recorded its output.

What broke.
(1) Closure, GF-CLOSE-2 with the closing round. A blocking finding raised by the critique on the closing tree T can be resolved "fixed" with a genuine frozen fix verification that has nothing to do with it. The pre-fix run uses an arbitrary older base where some unrelated test fails, and the post-fix run is on T, unchanged. The tree does not change and the defect remains in T. Battery 2 then runs, the slice closes and the GF audit is clean. The engine records fixVerify.base but never compares it with the tree of the finding's review, and it accepts a fixed finding inside the closing round. Design 16.5 says a closing round cannot carry a fixed finding. No forged event is needed; this is blocking.
(2) The clean-tree check uses git status, which does not see files marked skip-worktree. The reviewers and both batteries see the working copy, while every record names the committed tree, which can hold different code. Major.
(3) audit.run throws, against its "never throws" contract, when .claude/settings.json or .mcp.json is malformed. The cause is that preflight runs outside the audit's try. Major (a crash).
(4) The drafts branch of the GF policy skips the symlink resolution that GF-OWN-2 applies to project paths. One plain ln -s inside a group's own drafts namespace lets the Write/Edit file tools land in another group's files and in the event log. The hook's RECORD_FILES test reads only the literal path, so that row of the 16.4 table does not hold in the sandbox and guard profiles, where group roles have Bash. Major.
(5) Plain shell write commands that bashWriteTargets does not model (ln -sf, install, dd, perl -pi, touch, git checkout --, patch) let a group role write into another group's paths. This belongs to the text-level class, but none of these commands is obfuscated. Minor.

What held.
- Path normalisation (.., ./, //, absolute paths, NUL, backslash), and symlinks under project paths that point into another group or outside the project.
- The ownership glob algebra: covered() is sound for the glob syntax matchesAny supports, globsOverlap has no false negatives, and the reserved paths are protected.
- Rescope: the frozen rescope cannot change a task's owner. The group check runs before the frozen call, and the audit replays it.
- Completion: the GF-OWN-3 owner check in the audit, and the frozen claim and ownership checks.
- GF-FRZ-1 refuses non-api group roles and sealed contract files without an open request.
- GF-CONF-1 refuses group roles writing the three config paths by their literal path, and the audit reports drift after the latest pin.
- Closure records: a reused dispatch, a dispatch of another role or step, a review on an older tree, a reviewer that authored work, a proof reused for two findings, a battery not tied to its own run, a survivor list that does not match the evidence, late events on a closed scope, and every malformed accounting form I tried were all refused or reported.

What I did not count as findings.
- Forged events that are internally consistent and committed through Store.commit, including a forged mutation evidence followed by its battery. These are L-GF-17.
- Dispatch inputs copied out of the working record (L-GF-23).
- Reviewer independence being role-level only (L-GF-19).
- A re-pin by the orchestrator that loosens a config (L-GF-22).
- Interpreter writes from a shell (the hook is best-effort and text-level, L-GF-1).

Tests: the gf-close and gf-permissions suites pass (152 of 152) on the clone. No test covers findings 1 to 5.

findings.summary: A blocking critique finding raised on the closing tree is resolved 'fixed' with a real but unrelated fix-verify pair (pre-fix at an arbitrary older base fails, post-fix on the unchanged tree passes); the tree never changes, the defect stays, close succeeds and the GF audit is clean. closure.js:225-240 never ties fixVerify.base to the finding's review tree, and closure.js:341-382 accepts a fixed finding inside the closing round, contrary to design 16.5 ('a closing round cannot carry one'). Repro: repro-c2-1-fixed-without-fix.js

The clean-tree check (closure.js:43-49, git status --porcelain) is blind to files marked skip-worktree/assume-unchanged: the committed tree T differs from the working copy the reviewers read and the batteries mutate, yet dispatches, reviews, both batteries and the closure are recorded on T and the audit is clean. Repro: repro-c2-2-skip-worktree.js

audit.run is documented never to throw, but preflight runs outside its try (audit.js:180) and preflight.js:30-42 / install.protectionProfile read .claude/settings.json and .mcp.json unguarded: invalid JSON, a JSON null, a non-array PreToolUse or non-array args make audit.run, gf_audit and eccode-gf audit throw. Repro: repro-c2-3-audit-crash.js

permissions.js:300-303 returns for .eccode/drafts/<group>/ before resolveReal, and guard.js:458 tests RECORD_FILES on the literal path: after one plain 'ln -s' in its own drafts namespace (Bash is allowed in the sandbox and guard profiles), a group role's Write/Edit file-tool writes land in another group's files and in .eccode/events.jsonl, which the 16.4 table says the hook stops. Repros: repro-c2-4-drafts-symlink.js, repro-c2-4b-drafts-symlink-record.js

GF-OWN-2's shell half only judges the targets bashWriteTargets models (guard.js:86-122): plain, unobfuscated ln -sf, install, dd of=, perl -pi, touch, git checkout -- <path> and patch into another group's path are allowed for a group role (cp to the same path is denied); ln -sf lets frontend rewrite backend's app/main.py. Group roles keep Bash in the default sandbox profile. Repro: repro-c2-5-plain-shell-writes.js

data.summary:
R3 READINESS, scope S2, role architecture-reviewer, tree 010ac02 (checkout cloned to review-c3/copy). VERDICT: GO.

What I judged: whether every deliverable that design sections 16, 17.2 and 18 and the S2 plan promise for S2 exists in this tree and works, whether the tests pass, whether the frozen set is untouched, and whether the limits are registered. I did not judge S3 to S6 items. The engine enforces the record-level closing conditions at close time (two batteries, round-1 findings resolved, accounting), and on instruction I did not inspect the other reviews in the record.

Reasons for GO, each with its evidence:

1. Frozen set intact. phase2-seeds check prints "frozen: 48 files" (ev:ev-mw6oflxq-0120beca). The S2 commits 3f6ee65..HEAD change none of the 48 frozen files, docs/limits.md or scripts/guards (ev:ev-mw6ofm1v-016a212a). No frozen file requires lib/greenfield: the only frozen uses of the word "greenfield" are the track name.

2. Exit criterion 16.8 item 1 is met (docs/design/greenfield-senior.md:729). The full check (validate-toolkit plus every test) with ECCODE_PYTHON set to the FastAPI venv exits 0: 1410 tests, 1396 pass, 0 fail, exactly 14 skipped (ev:ev-mw6opou0-01309386). The 14 skips are the ones 16.8 names: 6 Mealie checkout, 4 ECCODE_MEALIE_VALIDATE, 1 realbugs, 1 ECCODE_CBM, 1 kotlinc, 1 codebase-memory-mcp. All 810 gf tests pass (ev:ev-mw6ohn4m-0164a063).

3. Ownership map and the five GF-OWN rules exist and pass their tests (ev:ev-mw6ogemn-017e4af0):
   - GF-OWN-1: the effective map with its glob algebra (lib/greenfield/ownership.js:70). The sealed bytes are hash-checked, and the audit checks every task.
   - GF-OWN-5: the reviewer amendment (lib/greenfield/ownership-ops.js:87) and the rescope check (lib/greenfield/ownership-ops.js:123).
   - GF-OWN-3: the completion check, including the task-owner check (lib/greenfield/ownership-ops.js:241). My probe that disables that check is killed (ev:ev-mw6ok406-018e4388).
   - GF-OWN-4: attribution, as a function, a CLI command and an MCP tool. Its audit integration is deferred to S4 and declared as such in 16.2 and 18.

4. GF-OWN-2, GF-FRZ-1, drafts namespacing and GF-CONF-1 are enforced in the real hook and covered by tests that run the hook (ev:ev-mw6ogl55-0189c348). Locations: lib/greenfield/permissions.js:41, called from scripts/hooks/guard.js:461. The GF-CONF-1 audit is at lib/greenfield/pin.js:43. The hook fails closed on a tampered breakdown.json. Bash write targets, symlinked directories and ".." paths are all judged. My probes that disable the FRZ-1 open-request check and the CONF-1 hook denial are both killed (ev:ev-mw6ok406-018e4388).

5. The closure rule GF-CLOSE-1 to 5 and the three-step review are built:
   - GF-CLOSE-5 dispatch: lib/greenfield/closure.js:62.
   - The closure check: lib/greenfield/closure.js:341.
   - Event schemas and the audit replay are in place.
   - 118 closure tests pass (ev:ev-mw6og9tw-01a9de68). Dispatch tree binding and the orchestrator-only dispatch are each pinned by a test (ev:ev-mw6ok406-018e4388).

6. The L-GF-17 preflight and the 56-pair spoof matrix exist and pass (lib/greenfield/preflight.js:29; ev:ev-mw6ogquf-01735dbe). The residual is restated in the register (docs/limits-greenfield.md:25).

7. The limits are registered: L-GF-19, L-GF-22 and L-GF-23 (docs/limits-greenfield.md:27, docs/limits-greenfield.md:30, docs/limits-greenfield.md:31). The docs tests pass (ev:ev-mw6ogr10-01d62269). S2 builds and claims none of GF-PRE, GF-UX, gf.tool.run, gf.slice.opened or attestation: none of them appears in lib or bin.

Residuals that do not block GO (the rules work; these are gaps in tests or text):

a) Two clauses of the closure rule are not pinned by any shipped test:
   - "the first battery is recorded before the first review" (lib/greenfield/closure.js:370);
   - authorship through a completion or a gate submission (lib/greenfield/closure.js:59).
   Disabling either one leaves gf-close and gf-review-s2 green (ev:ev-mw6oin7q-018ba3f4). Plan step 127 listed "completed a task or submitted to a gate" as a negative row (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-07-greenfield-senior-s2.md:127), but the tree tests only a claim (tests/gf-close.test.js:121). The test titled "late review" forges only a late dispatch (tests/gf-close.test.js:437). My own probe confirms that the code behaves as designed on all of these paths (ev:ev-mw6ohobs-013d460e). I recommend adding these tests.

b) Readiness evidence accepts only checks that passed or were recorded (lib/greenfield/closure.js:118). A no-go verdict therefore cannot cite a failing executed check, only path:line.

c) A code comment still calls the preflight "a recorded fact" (lib/greenfield/preflight.js:5). Section 18 says it is computed each time.

d) Section 18 cites docs/build/gf-s2-evidence.md, which is not yet in the tree (docs/design/greenfield-senior.md:885). The ledger's S2 row is "pending" (docs/build/compute-ledger.md:28). Both are post-close step 5 of 16.8, so this is expected.

**What a spoof buys.** (1) Writes: an A agent acting as B can claim B's tasks and write B's files; the attribution of a change is per claim, never per author (L-GF-3 is the same fact inside a group). (2) Reviewer-only events (`gf.ownership.amended`, finding resolutions, closure reviews): an A agent acting as a reviewer could amend the map or close its own slice. What a spoof does **not** buy: the sealed contracts, the pinned guard configs and the sealed acceptance tests are content-addressed (GF-FRZ-2, GF-CONF-1, GF-ACC-2): any change to them is detected whoever made it.
    
    **Minimal fix, in S2 (no secret needed).** (F0) A *managed-path preflight*: `eccode-gf preflight` and a section of `eccode-gf audit` report which regime is in force (computed from the current settings each time; it is not a log event, so it says nothing about the regime when an earlier event was committed): the install profile (`sandbox`, `no-shell` or `guard`), whether the guard is wired for `mcp__eccode_.*` and the file tools, and whether each group role has a role-locked server entry. `guard` profile or a missing wiring is reported as a **warning that names the consequence** ("a group can act as another undetectably"); `eccode-gf verify-done` (S5) will print the regime in the delivery report. (F1) Make the S2 ownership rules lean on facts the actor string does not decide: GF-OWN-4 attributes paths to the task owners' groups through the map in force (sealed plus valid amendments), and GF-OWN-3 reads the completing actor and the task's owner: the actor must be the task's owner (a fact of the reviewed plan), and the listed files must belong to the actor's group, so a forged completion of another group's task is reported. A spoofed actor completing its own group's work still passes; that is L-GF-17. (F2) Say it plainly in the register: L-GF-17 is re-stated with the exact residual.
    
    **Proposed, not built, for the owner's decision.** (F3) *Keyed attestation*: `eccode-gf init` generates a per-role key stored outside the repository and handed to each role-locked server; after each commit the server appends `gf.attest {seq, hash, role, mac}`; the audit verifies the MAC and flags a group-role event without a valid attestation. That turns "a forged actor is undetectable" into "a forged actor is detected unless the agent read the key". Cost: about 250 lines, key management, and the key directory must be read-denied to agents, which only works where the harness runs hooks on Read (the same best-effort class as L-GF-7). Recommended for S5, next to done-verification, which should refuse DONE on an unattested group event. It does not help the plain CLI and does not protect against a defeated hook that also reads the key.

data.summary:
S2 enforces S1's sealed ownership map as path-scoped permissions, pins the guard configurations, and makes slice closure an engine rule. No frozen file is edited; enforcement sits at the eccode-gf/MCP wrappers (P), the hook (H) and the audit (A).

Ownership map. Each read checks the approved breakdown.json against the seal hashes, then applies gf.ownership.amended events in order ("from" must equal the globs in force; "to" replaces them; nothing else changes). Every map must keep groups disjoint under a conservative glob algebra, give contracts/** and mocks/** to api and tests/acceptance/** to test, and strand no pending or claimed task. A path belongs to the group whose globs match it and whose denyGlobs do not; otherwise it has no owner.
- GF-OWN-1: every task's owner is in a group and its files lie in that group's globs (checked at the seal and by the audit). After the seal, a hash mismatch makes the hook deny all group-role writes.
- GF-OWN-2 (hook): a group role writes only inside its group's globs and a claimed task's globs; unowned paths are refused.
- GF-OWN-3: the completer is the task's owner, and the listed files are in its group.
- GF-OWN-4: changed paths are attributed to completed tasks of the owning group. In S2 this is a command; the audit uses it from S4.
- GF-OWN-5: only a reviewer amendment with a reason and a cited message changes the map, and a rescope cannot leave the group.
Before the seal, the claimed-task rule decides. GF-FRZ-1: only api writes contract files, and after the seal only while an amendment request for that file is open. Group roles write drafts only under .eccode/drafts/<group>/.

Guard-config pin. GF-CONF-1: gf.config.pinned (orchestrator or user) hashes behavior.json, guards.json and security.json. The latest pin is the reference, and any later change, deletion or new file is drift. Group roles may not write them; a loosened file re-pinned is recorded, not refused.

Closure. The orchestrator or user commits gf.slice.closed only if all of these hold on a clean HEAD^{tree}:
- Each of the three steps (comprehension, critique, readiness) has a valid review on that tree, each with its own earlier dispatch (role, step, tree, hashed inputs, working-record paths refused, one review per dispatch).
- Reviewers are reviewer roles that authored nothing and are not the closer.
- Readiness is go and cites resolvable evidence.
- Every finding is resolved: fixed (proven by a fix-verify, or by a paired run for documentation findings); withdrawn by the role that raised it; or deferred by the user (minor findings only, with a limit id). A fixed finding forces a new round.
- At least two mutation batteries exist: the first before the first review, the last on the closing tree after the last fix, with a reason for each survivor.
- The accounting has a form-valid start and end.
A closed scope accepts nothing more. S2 is closed this way, in a fresh record.

Identity. The log asserts actors and does not bind them. On the managed path, A can act as B only if the role-locked servers (with the harness tool list) or the hook fail. The log cannot show their failure afterwards, so the documents call ownership spoofable in that sense. Built in S2: a preflight that reports the current regime (not a log event), rules that lean on the plan's task owners and the map, and a restated L-GF-17. Keyed attestation is proposed for S5, not built.

Accounting. The unit is input, output, cache-read and cache-write tokens summed, from a cumulative harness snapshot at slice start and end. The ledger has one row per slice and per delegated agent: agent figures are "as reported", missing ones "unmeasurable". GF-CLOSE-4 checks only the form.

Not guaranteed:
- sub-agents within a group are indistinguishable;
- drafts are readable, and dispatch prompts are out of band;
- once the controls fail, a spoof cannot be detected, and a spoofed role's amendments and re-pins are recorded, not flagged;
- reviewer independence is role-level, and zero context is attested;
- the tree carries the authors' conclusions;
- an unlisted cross-group write is found only by attribute;
- closure checks form, not truth;
- a closure ignores later commits.

findings.summary: 16.5 'How S2 itself is closed' and 16.8 item 4 say the record is 'initialised inside a separate checkout of the final tree'; 16.8 item 4 adds 'round 1, its findings, their proofs and battery 1 are in the same record'. But 16.8 item 3 and 17.2 'Order in a slice' put battery 1 and round 1 on the build tree, before any fix, so before the final tree exists. Plan Task 7 instead says 'a record beside a checkout of the final tree'. The documents do not say when the record is initialised, whether it sits inside or beside the checkout, or how a checkout of the final tree gives a HEAD^{tree} equal to the build tree for battery 1 and round 1. (Presumably the checkout is moved from commit to commit, but no document says so.)

The 16.5 amendment note says 'the latest review' below reads 'a review of each step on the closing tree, readiness go', but the phrase 'the latest review' no longer appears in 16.5. GF-CLOSE-1 says 'a valid review of that step' and 'the readiness verdict go' (singular). Nothing says whether a step may be dispatched more than once on the same tree, or which review counts if it is. A readiness review carries no findings (17.2: 'none'), so GF-CLOSE-2 does not keep a no-go alive. The documents do not say whether a later go on the same tree overrides an earlier no-go, or whether every readiness review on the closing tree must be go.

Section 18 'Precedence' makes only section 18 and 'the clarifications in section 16 marked as coming after a review' normative, because 'section 16 was written before the build'. But unmarked text in section 16 already holds as-built content: 16.2 GF-OWN-3 'as built; the owner half came from the round-1 review'; 16.4 F0 'it is not a log event', which 18 calls '16.4 F0 now'; 16.5 GF-CLOSE-1 'a fixed finding needs a new round', which 18 lists as round-2 C2-1. The plan's unamended steps contradict that content, and section 18 does not mention the conflict. Plan Task 5 Step 1 lists 'verdict findings (GF-CLOSE-1)' as a refusal, while 16.5 GF-CLOSE-1 lets a closing comprehension or critique review 'list findings only if each is withdrawn or deferred'. The documents do not say which governs where unmarked section-16 text and the plan differ, so a reader of the plan would build a clean-only closing review.

GF-OWN-1 is stated inconsistently. (a) Which map and which tasks: 16.3 judges 'pending and claimed tasks: their files lie inside the group's effective globs now' (completed tasks: owner only). Plan Task 1 Step 3 judges 'every engine task (owner in a group, files inside the group at the seal or the last rescope)'. Section 18 says nothing. (b) Enforcement points: the 16.2 table gives GF-OWN-1 'P (seal), A'. Yet the 16.2 clarification and plan Task 2 have the hook deny group-role writes 'with the GF-OWN-1 reason' after the seal when the sealed breakdown fails its hash check. That is an H point the table leaves out.

The 16.5 table row 'closed is closed' has no rule id, unlike every other closure condition, although plan Task 5 Step 1 requires 'rule id and fragment each' for its negative row 'scope already closed'. The row also covers 'a review, resolution or battery' but not a gf.dispatch.recorded for a closed scope, so it is not stated whether a late dispatch is refused. Separately, the 16.5 heading and 16.1 item 1 still say 'GF-CLOSE-1 to 4', and plan Task 5 commits 'GF-CLOSE-1..4', while the rule set is GF-CLOSE-1 to 5. That part is recoverable from the amendment note.

16.4 F1 says the S2 ownership rules 'lean on facts the actor string does not decide'. But GF-OWN-3's own condition, 'the actor must be the task's owner', is decided by the actor string: a writer who forges the actor as the task's owner passes, as the same paragraph concedes ('A spoofed actor completing its own group's work still passes'), and as plan Task 6's residual concedes. So 'a forged completion of another group's task is reported' holds only when the forger does not also forge the actor, which is exactly the L-GF-17 case. The documents do not say plainly what F1 adds against a writer who controls the actor string.

'Managed path' is used in two senses. Section 2.2 and the enforcement wording (limits header, L-GF-1) define it as the MCP / eccode-gf write path (point P), and 16.4's vector table marks an Edit/Write file write as 'any', not 'managed'. Yet L-GF-24 says a cross-group file write 'is refused by the hook on the managed path', and the 16.4 Finding counts the PreToolUse hook among the controls of the managed path. So the documents do not say consistently whether GF-OWN-2 (a hook rule on the file tools) is a managed-path prevention or a best-effort hook check, or in which profiles.

GF-CONF-1 (16.2 clarification) says 'the latest pin, whatever its scope, is the reference', and in S2 a pin is made only by 'eccode-gf config pin'. The documents do not say what the audit reports for a Greenfield-Senior project with no gf.config.pinned at all (a problem, or nothing checked). They also do not say what the pin's 'scope' field means or whether it is checked. Plan Task 4 also refuses 'a reason under 10 characters', a minimum that neither 16.2 nor section 7 states.

16.5 'Records, stated precisely' says an 'ev:<id> resolves when that evidence exists, precedes the review and passed or was recorded'. 'Was recorded' is never defined: every existing evidence was recorded, and if it means an evidence status called 'recorded', that status is never defined. So the condition for a valid readiness citation, other than 'passed', cannot be reconstructed.

16.5 'Definitions' requires that 'A fix-verify's base commit must have the tree the finding was raised on', and section 18 (C2-1) says 'a fix proof is of the reviewed tree'. But the list of what the engine checks for a paired run has no tree condition. That list is: equal commands after whitespace normalisation, a failed reproduction recorded with purpose reproduction after the finding's review, a passing proof after it, both before the resolution. The documents do not say whether a paired run's reproduction must run on the reviewed tree, or on which tree its passing run must be.

16.5 'How S2 itself is closed' says 'the repository's own tracked .eccode/ is moved aside there, which the tree identity excludes'. But the tree identity is HEAD^{tree} (GF-CLOSE-1; plan Task 5 Step 3), the commit's tree object, and that object contains every tracked path, a tracked .eccode/ included. What excludes .eccode/ is the clean-tree check ('Clean tree', 16.5). A reader cannot tell whether a closure's treeHash is the commit's tree or a tree with .eccode/ removed.

Scoring of the S2 estimate is defined two ways, and incompletely. 16.7 counts tests with 'table rows now counted', while 17.9 says 'Tests' means 'the # tests count of node --test'. Rows checked in a loop inside one test() are not counted in '# tests', so the two definitions give different numbers against the registered range of 130 to 260. Also, 17.9 registers prediction P7, but plan Task 7 Step 5 scores only 'the registered predictions P4 to P6'.

The 16.7 token row says 'S2 starts with about 146 k of context rather than several hundred thousand'. That is the stated reason the 40 to 150 M registration may sit below S1's measured 129.5 M, but no source or measurement is given for the 146 k figure, whereas the snapshots in 16.6 name their files.

16.2 says GF-OWN-2 'fails closed in a Greenfield-Senior project', and plan Task 2 says a null policy 'means the project is not a Greenfield-Senior project' and the existing hook rules apply unchanged. The documents do not say how the hook decides that a project is a Greenfield-Senior project, or what it does when it cannot decide (for example, when the log is unreadable). So the condition under which the fail-closed ownership check is skipped altogether is not stated.

data.summary:
R2 critique of S2 (design sections 16, 17 and 18; plan 2026-11-07-greenfield-senior-s2.md; limits L-GF-1 to 27), by security-reviewer on a private clone of the dispatched tree. Every reproduction is a node script under review-d2/repro/ that builds a sealed project from the repository's own fixtures (tests/fixtures/gf/flow.js, close.js), runs the real hook as a child process or calls the closure and audit functions, and prints its observed result.

What I attacked. (1) The hook's write check (GF-OWN-2, GF-FRZ-1, GF-CONF-1, the drafts namespace) through the file tools: relative and absolute paths, '..' normalisation, symlinks inside the project, and paths outside the project that resolve inside it. (2) The clean-tree definition behind GF-CLOSE-1, 3 and 5: index flags, repository configuration, untracked files. (3) The closure rule: independence (authorship, closer as reviewer), dispatch inputs and their refused paths, step verdicts, superseded reviews, proof reuse, battery binding and survivors, accounting form, closed-is-closed. (4) The audit: schema-valid forged gf.* and engine events committed through Store.commit, to see whether it throws or misses them. (5) Whether the tests fail when a check is removed.

What broke. D2-1 (blocking): a file-tool write to /proc/self/root followed by the project's absolute path is never judged. guard.js treats it as outside the project before the Greenfield policy runs, so the group-glob rule, the sealed-contract rule, the guard-config rule and even the record-file rule are skipped. The bytes land in the project file. This needs no shell. D2-2 (major): the clean tree depends on local git config. With status.showUntrackedFiles=no an untracked, non-ignored file is hidden, and a dispatch, review, battery or closure is recorded as being on a clean tree. D2-3 (minor): a readiness no-go on the closing tree is erased by a later go on the same tree. D2-4 (minor): a committed symlinked directory lets a dispatch list a handoff, because inputs are refused by textual path only. D2-5 (minor): one forged engine event with a non-list 'files' stops the audit at the ownership section. Every later rule section is then unreported. ok stays false, so the audit still fails closed.

What held. Ownership algebra: overlapping or unprovable globs are refused, and '..', absolute and backslash paths are rejected. A symlink inside the project is judged where it lands (C2-4). Amendments and rescopes are replayed against the map in force. The audit returned without throwing on every forged closure, dispatch, battery and amendment I committed, and reported each one: 23 errors in the control run. The closure refuses a missing step, a no-go as the only readiness, a dispatch reused or for another role, step or tree, and a direct .eccode/handoffs input. Rule-removal checks: removing the C2-2 index-flag check fails 2 tests. Removing the authorship check fails 3, and judging drafts paths without resolving symlinks fails 3. The tests do catch these checks being removed.

Not filed. Shell-text analysis is admitted as text-level (the guard header, limits rows 91 and 117, the design's 'best-effort' wording), so I did not catalogue shell forms. Actor spoofing through forged events is L-GF-17. The battery's command choice and the accounting figures are L-GF-26. Note, not a defect: install.js gives role agents Bash in the sandbox profile (giveRoleTools shell: true). Design 2.2 says sandbox agents have no shell, and preflight reports that profile as managed-path.

findings.summary: The hook does not judge a file-tool write whose path is textually outside the project but resolves inside it: scripts/hooks/guard.js:481 returns null ('outside the project') before lib/greenfield/permissions.js (resolveReal, policy) is reached. A Write to /proc/self/root<abs project path>/<rel> is allowed for frontend-engineer on app/main.py (GF-OWN-2) and contracts/openapi.json (GF-FRZ-1), and for backend-engineer on .eccode/security.json (GF-CONF-1), .eccode/events.jsonl (record) and .claude/settings.json (hook wiring), all denied by their direct path; the write lands in the project file. No shell is needed, so it holds in the no-shell profile too; the audit sees the cross-group write only if a completion lists it (L-GF-24). Reproduction: repro/r1-proc-root.js (5/5 denied writes become allowed).

The clean-tree check is weaker than design 16.5 states ('untracked files that are not ignored count as dirty'): lib/greenfield/closure.js:46 (treeState) runs git status with the repository's local config, so 'git config status.showUntrackedFiles no' (in .git/config, not in the tree) hides an untracked, non-ignored file. treeState reports clean, and a dispatch is recorded on that tree; the same applies to reviews, batteries and the closure, which use the same check. Reproduction: repro/r2-clean-tree.js (control: dirty=[docs/extra.py]; with the setting: dirty=null, dispatch recorded).

A readiness no-go on the closing tree is overridden by any later readiness go on the same tree: lib/greenfield/closure.js:369-371 keeps only the latest valid readiness review per tree, and nothing requires the earlier no-go to be answered, while critique findings must each be resolved even after a later clean critique. The orchestrator can re-dispatch readiness until it reads go. Reproduction: repro/r3-nogo-superseded.js (close refused with 'readiness verdict ... is no-go'; after a second readiness go on the same tree the closure is accepted, steps.readiness names the go, GF audit 0 errors).

GF-CLOSE-5 refuses working-record inputs by their textual path only: lib/greenfield/closure.js:83-85 matches FORBIDDEN on the normalised string and recordDispatch (closure.js:103-107) lstat-checks only the last component. With a committed symlink docs/h -> ../.eccode/handoffs, a dispatch listing docs/h/ho-1.json is recorded and hashed (the design's GF-CLOSE-5 bypass row 'a dispatch listing .eccode/handoffs/' must fail); the direct path is refused; the audit reports nothing. Reproduction: repro/r4-dispatch-symlink-dir.js.

One forged engine event (task.rescoped with files: 5, committed through Store.commit) makes the GF audit stop at the ownership section (lib/greenfield/ownership-ops.js:249, 'for (const f of t.files)', 't.files is not iterable'); the shared try/catch in lib/greenfield/audit.js:41-176 then skips GF-CONF-1, GF-CLOSE-1..5 and GF-MSG, so their violations are not reported (ok stays false, so it fails closed). Reproduction: repro/r5-audit-abort.js (1 error, GF-AUD-1) against repro/r5b-audit-control.js (same forged events without the rescope: 23 errors across GF-OWN-5, GF-CLOSE-1..5).

(3) the rule-removal battery, my own scratch script that removes one rule id at a time, is extra evidence about my tests and does not satisfy GF-CLOSE-3. "At least two failing tests per rule" is what I expect of my tests, not a rule.
    
    **Clean tree.** `git status --porcelain` is empty outside `.eccode/`: tracked changes and untracked files that are not ignored count as dirty; `.eccode/` holds the record and is excluded, and the guard configurations inside it are covered by GF-CONF-1, not by the tree check. A closure is a record of the tree it names: a later commit does not undo it, but slice integration (S4) and DONE (S5) judge the current tree, and "no commit after it other than evidence" is my discipline, not an engine check.

The record is new, and in a fresh record the authorship condition holds trivially, because the build's claims and completions are not in it: independence is shown there only by the dispatches and the reviewer roles.

**What a spoof buys.** (1) Writes: an A agent acting as B can claim B's tasks and write B's files; the attribution of a change is per claim, never per author (L-GF-3 is the same fact inside a group). (2) Reviewer-only events (`gf.ownership.amended`, finding resolutions, closure reviews): an A agent acting as a reviewer could amend the map or close its own slice. What a spoof does **not** buy: the sealed contracts, the pinned guard configs and the sealed acceptance tests are content-addressed (GF-FRZ-2, GF-CONF-1, GF-ACC-2): a change outside their recorded change paths is detected whoever made it; a change made through a recorded change path (a contract amendment or an acceptance amendment by a spoofed reviewer, a re-pin by a spoofed orchestrator) is recorded but not flagged.
    
    **Minimal fix, in S2 (no secret needed).** (F0) A *managed-path preflight*: `eccode-gf preflight` and a section of `eccode-gf audit` report which regime is in force (computed from the current settings each time; it is not a log event, so it says nothing about the regime when an earlier event was committed): the install profile (`sandbox`, `no-shell` or `guard`), whether the guard is wired for `mcp__eccode_.*` and the file tools, and whether each group role has a role-locked server entry. `guard` profile or a missing wiring is reported as a **warning that names the consequence** ("a group can act as another undetectably"); `eccode-gf verify-done` (S5) will print the regime in the delivery report. (F1) Make the S2 ownership rules lean on facts the actor string does not decide: GF-OWN-4 attributes paths to the task owners' groups through the map in force (sealed plus valid amendments), and GF-OWN-3 reads the completing actor and the task's owner: the actor must be the task's owner (a fact of the reviewed plan), and the listed files must belong to the actor's group, so a forged completion of another group's task is reported. A spoofed actor completing its own group's work still passes; that is L-GF-17. (F2) Say it plainly in the register: L-GF-17 is re-stated with the exact residual.
    
    **Proposed, not built, for the owner's decision.** (F3) *Keyed attestation*: `eccode-gf init` generates a per-role key stored outside the repository and handed to each role-locked server; after each commit the server appends `gf.attest {seq, hash, role, mac}`; the audit verifies the MAC and flags a group-role event without a valid attestation. That turns "a forged actor is undetectable" into "a forged actor is detected unless the agent read the key". Cost: about 250 lines, key management, and the key directory must be read-denied to agents, which only works where the harness runs hooks on Read (the same best-effort class as L-GF-7). Recommended for S5, next to done-verification, which should refuse DONE on an unattested group event. It does not help the plain CLI and does not protect against a defeated hook that also reads the key.
