data.summary:
S2 makes the Greenfield-Senior groups real ownership domains and adds an engine rule for closing a slice.

Ownership map. The map is the groups of the sealed breakdown.json (name, roles, globs, denyGlobs), checked against the seal's hashes on every read. Reviewer amendments (gf.ownership.amended) are applied in log order; each replaces one group's globs, and its "from" must equal the globs in force. Each resulting map passes the GF-WBS-2 checks, now shared in ownership.js: groups disjoint, contracts/** and mocks/** to api, tests/acceptance/** to test. Globs of two groups may overlap only when one is provably inside the other and the outer group denies it; anything unprovable is refused. Amendments change globs only and cannot strand a pending or claimed task. A path belongs to the group whose globs match it and whose denyGlobs do not.

Enforcement points: P (MCP and eccode-gf wrappers), H (PreToolUse hook), A (audit replay), plus a command.
- GF-OWN-1: owners are in groups, and open tasks lie inside current globs. After the seal the hook fails closed if the breakdown hash fails or the policy cannot be evaluated.
- GF-OWN-2 (hook, permissions.js): a group role's write must lie inside its group's globs and a claimed task's globs. Unowned paths are refused.
- GF-OWN-3 (wrapped task_complete; audit at the map in force): the completer is the task's owner, and every listed file belongs to its group.
- GF-OWN-4: changed paths are attributed to completing tasks of the owning group. In S2 it is a function and "eccode-gf attribute"; the audit gets it in S4.
- GF-OWN-5: amendments come from a reviewer with a reason and a cited message, and rescopes stay inside the group.
- GF-FRZ-1 (hook): the six contract files are api-only, and after the seal writable only while an amendment request for the file is open.
- Drafts: group roles write only to .eccode/drafts/<group>/**.
A record with gf.project.initialized makes a project Greenfield-Senior for the hook; if the hook cannot decide, it fails closed. Before the seal, group roles hold no claims, so the claimed-task rule answers.

Guard-config pin (GF-CONF-1). gf.config.pinned (orchestrator or user, reason of 10+ characters, free scope label) hashes behavior.json, guards.json and security.json. The audit reports any change or new file after the latest pin. The hook refuses group-role writes even unpinned. A loosening re-pin is recorded, not refused (L-GF-22).

Closure (GF-CLOSE-1..5). The orchestrator or user commits gf.slice.closed, checked inside the lock and replayed by the audit. The closing tree (HEAD^{tree}, clean outside .eccode/) needs:
- valid reviews of three steps: comprehension (documentation findings), critique (defect findings) and readiness (go or no-go with resolvable citations);
- for each review, its own prior orchestrator dispatch (role, step, tree, hashed inputs; working-record paths refused);
- reviewers who are configured reviewer roles, authored nothing and are not the closer;
- readiness go, with no standing no-go;
- every finding resolved: fixed by fix-verify (for documentation, a paired fail-then-pass run), withdrawn by its raiser, or deferred by the user if minor. A fixed finding forces a new round on a new tree;
- at least two mutation batteries: the first before the first review, the last on the closing tree after the last fix, with reasons for its survivors;
- accounting in all-processed tokens, each figure an integer or "unmeasurable".
Nothing more is recorded for a closed scope.

Identity. The log asserts actors and does not bind them. One group cannot act as another only while the per-role server lock (with the harness tool list) and the hook hold; the preflight reports the current regime but cannot see a past failure. The documents conclude that ownership is spoofable in that sense. They build the preflight, check the completer against the planned owner, restate L-GF-17, and propose keyed attestation for S5.

Accounting. Harness cumulative totals (input, output, cache reads and writes) are snapshotted at slice start and end, with one ledger row per slice and per delegated agent; a missing figure reads "unmeasurable".

Not guaranteed: actor binding (L-GF-17); the reviewer's zero context, which is only attested (L-GF-19); authors' views in the tree (L-GF-23); cross-group writes no completion lists (L-GF-24); truthful accounting and battery parameters (L-GF-26); the tree after closure (L-GF-27); which tree a paired run saw (L-GF-28); anything with hooks off.

findings.summary: Sections 2.2 and 16.4 contradict each other on which install profiles give group roles a shell. Section 2.2 says 'in `sandbox` the record is read-only to shell commands' and 'a shell write (group roles have a shell in the `sandbox` and `guard` profiles) is judged on its command text only'. The 16.4 vector table says '`eccode --actor B ...` | `guard` profile only (the other profiles have no shell)'. 16.4 says it will 'Enumerate every way' but has no row for a shell write of group B's files, which 2.2 and L-GF-24 treat as text-judged only. F0 warns only for the `guard` profile. A reader cannot tell whether the sandbox profile's text-level shell checks belong to the regime the preflight must report.

16.2 'Which projects the hook treats as Greenfield-Senior' (and plan Task 2 `policy`) gives two outcomes. 'No initialised record, or a record without that event, means the project is not Greenfield-Senior': the existing rules apply, so the hook fails open. When 'the record cannot be opened or its log cannot be read or replayed, it fails closed'. Neither 'initialised record' nor 'cannot be opened' is defined, so the line between failing open and failing closed cannot be reconstructed. For example, an `.eccode/` that exists while its `events.jsonl` is missing, empty or moved aside could fall on either side.

16.5 (L-GF-19 paragraph) says 'the rule gives no way to record them as one: a review is recorded only by a reviewer role, over MCP or `eccode-gf`, with the actor locked'. L-GF-19 says 'An author's own bypass tests are never recorded as a review pass'. Both contradict 16.4. There the log asserts the actor, and a CLI `--actor B` is stopped only by the text-level hook in the `guard` profile, or by nothing when the harness sends no `agent_type` (15.1 M1 treats `eccode-gf` as the eccode CLI). Item (2) of 'What a spoof buys' says a spoofed reviewer can record closure reviews. The documents do not say that GF-CLOSE-1's reviewer-role and not-the-closer conditions rest on the assumptions of L-GF-17. They also do not say which path a closing review must take. L-GF-19 names only the 'two instances of one role' residual.

16.4 'What a spoof buys' says 'Reviewer-only events (`gf.ownership.amended`, finding resolutions, closure reviews): an A agent acting as a reviewer could amend the map or close its own slice'. But 16.5 says 'any actor may record a fixed resolution', deferral is 'only by `user`', and 'The orchestrator or the user commits `gf.slice.closed`'. Resolutions are not reviewer-only, and a reviewer cannot close a slice. The stated reach of a spoof therefore does not match the rules: closing needs a spoofed orchestrator or user, and a fixed resolution needs no spoof at all.

18 'Precedence' gives the order 'this section; then section 16 and section 17.2 as they now stand; then the plan'. That order does not place the rest of the design (sections 2 to 15, 17.1, 17.3 to 17.9), and it ranks 16 and 17.2 equally, so a conflict between them is not ordered. Section 8 still gives GF-FRZ-1 as 'H,P,A', while 16.2 says 'no P point'. Section 8 also says GF-CONF-1 'guard configs pinned per slice' at 'slice,A', while 16.2 says 'H, A' and 'the latest pin, whatever its scope, is the reference'. 16.2 lists its deviations only 'from section 4.2'.

16.5 says 'Only records that pass their own checks count', but the design does not fully state what makes a review record valid. (1) 17.2 requires 'a summary of at least 100 characters' only for comprehension, while the plan's as-built block requires 'summary (>= 100)' for every review. (2) The severity values blocking, major and minor appear only in the plan's superseded interface; section 7 lists `severity` without values. (3) 'verdict is clean iff no findings' also appears only in that superseded interface. (4) 16.5 says 'the kind follows the step', yet each finding carries a `kind`, and nothing says whether a mismatched kind is refused or overridden. (5) 17.2 says readiness has 'none' findings, yet 18 cites 'the readiness reviewer's residual, D3-1' without saying what kind of record D3-1 is or whether a readiness review may carry findings.

Battery survivors: 16.5 ('Three things are called a battery') says 'every survivor of the last battery needs an accepted reason or a test that kills it'. GF-CLOSE-3 says 'its survivors listed with a reason each, or none', with the reasons in `gf.slice.closed.accepted`. A test that kills a survivor changes the tree, so that battery is no longer the last one on the closing tree. The documents do not say whether the engine accepts the 'test' alternative at all. The `round` field of `gf.battery.recorded` (section 7; the plan says 'integer >= 1') has no stated meaning and no stated check.

Battery numbers: 16.5 says 'at most `max`, 25 by default', but 18 reports 'The third (tree `faa7031a`, 19 of 20 killed)' and says 'a tree that adds only tests is mutated in the same 20 places'. No `--max` value or reason for 20 is given. 16.8 says 'engine battery run 2 on the final tree' and 17.2 'the second battery on that tree'. In 18, however, battery 2 ran on `f7b3db2` and battery 3 on `faa7031a`, and a test was added after that. The documents do not say which battery is, or will be, bound to the final tree.

`.eccode/` paths under GF-OWN-3 and GF-OWN-4: plan Task 3 says '`completionProblems` ... `.eccode/` paths ignored'. Design 16.2 states no such exception: GF-OWN-3 requires that 'every listed changed file belongs to the actor's group', and GF-OWN-4 covers 'every path changed since a base commit'. 16.2's '`.eccode/` paths are left to the hook's record rules' concerns writes only. Section 18 supersedes the plan's interfaces, so a reader cannot tell whether a completion that lists `.eccode/drafts/<group>/x` is refused. A reader also cannot tell whether attribution covers changes to tracked `.eccode/` files.

GF-OWN-5's conditions are incomplete. The minimum reason length, 'reason (>= 30)', appears only in plan Task 1. Design 4.2, 16.2 and section 7 say only 'with a reason' or `reason`, and 18 says section 7 supersedes the plan's interfaces. 'A cited message' (section 7: '`message` a recorded message') states no condition on the message's kind, sender or recipient. Section 4.5 requires that 'an amendment, an escalation, or a rescope must cite a message id'. Yet the S2 rescope wrapper (16.2; plan Task 1 `rescope`) checks only the group, and no section says the rescope's message citation is deferred.

16.6 says 'A restart that resets the cumulative counter makes `end` lower than `start`; the snapshot that crosses it is recorded as `unmeasurable`'. A reset gives end < start only if usage after the restart stays below start. Otherwise a wrong figure passes GF-CLOSE-4's 'end >= start' check. 'The snapshot that crosses it' also does not say whether start or end is recorded as `unmeasurable`.

16.7 registered P4 ('The first independent pass finds at least three defects of major or blocking severity in the S2 code') and P5 ('The second pass, on the post-fix tree') for one review per pass. Since 17.2, a round has two or three steps, comprehension findings are documentation rather than code, and 18 shows three rounds. 17.9 says 'Predictions P4 to P6 stand as registered' but does not say which steps' findings count or which round is 'the second pass'. Plan Task 7 Step 5 requires scoring these predictions, and the documents do not give the scoring rule.

Owner decision 16.1, item 1(b), requires that 'every finding [be] reproduced as a failing test before any fix'. The 16.5 paired run accepts 'one command (normally a test of the document)'. The engine 'does not check that the failure was an assertion', and no check ties the command to the finding. The documents do not record this as a deviation from a binding owner decision. The limits register (L-GF-26, L-GF-28) names only the form and tree residuals.

17.5 says 'the redacted output is stored; a raw output that could hold a secret is hashed in memory and never persisted'. 17.8 item 7 says 'every other tool's raw output is hashed and stored as it is'. The two disagree for tools other than Gitleaks whose output can quote source. An example is Semgrep, which 17.5 maps to a 'secrets' guard class: one section says its raw output is never persisted, the other that it is stored as it is. This is registered for S4a.

data.summary:
Critique (R2) of S2 by security-reviewer, on the final tree 21ef6eb (tree bceec2cbe263030da0148c65c79bac2c0bb23b67), cloned into review-e2/copy. Inputs read: design sections 2, 16, 17 and 18, the S2 plan, docs/limits-greenfield.md, and the code of lib/greenfield (permissions, ownership, ownership-ops, closure, audit, events, projection, pin, preflight, index), scripts/hooks/guard.js, lib/project.js, lib/fixverify.js and lib/mutate.js. The slice's own permission, review, attribution and spoof tests pass on this tree (185 of 185), so the failures below are not environmental. Every reproduction is a node test under review-e2/repro that runs the real hook or the real module against a throwaway sealed project built with the slice's own fixtures (tests/fixtures/gf/flow.js). Each test asserts the behaviour the design states and fails on this tree.

What broke. The main weakness is the hook's model of plain shell writers, which the design calls best effort (L-GF-1, 2.2) but which round 2 (C2-5) extended explicitly. (E2-1) mv deletes its source, but only the destination is judged. A backend role removes a frontend file, the guard config .eccode/security.json and a sealed contract, while rm of each is denied. (E2-2) Hard links (ln, cp -l) are judged on the link name only. A backend role links another group's file, a guard config or a sealed contract into its own path and then writes it. A file-tool Write to the link is allowed too, and an in-place write lands on the sealed contract. (E2-3) A cd separated by ';' or a newline is dropped, and pushd is not modelled, so 'cd app; echo x > ../web/index.html' is judged as a write outside the project and allowed. (E2-4) A subagent's git apply, git mv and git rm are not modelled. On the detection side, (E2-5) eccode-gf attribute (GF-OWN-4) uses git diff --name-only, whose rename detection reports a committed cross-group move under the new name only. The frontend removal is never attributed and attribute exits 0, which contradicts L-GF-24. Together with E2-1, a cross-group deletion is neither refused nor found. Smaller findings: (E2-6) a dispatch input hard-linked to .eccode/events.jsonl is accepted, though the symlink form is refused (D2-4). (E2-7) the clean-tree check still honours core.excludesFile and .git/info/exclude, so an untracked source file outside the reviewed tree counts as clean. (E2-8) the preflight reports managed-path when the project's settings turn the guard off (an env entry ECCODE_HOOKS=off, or disableAllHooks). That last one is shown at the report level only: I did not verify the harness's handling of those settings.

What held. File-tool writes across groups, unowned paths, contract files without an open request, the three config files, the drafts namespace, symlinked files and directories, '..' and absolute routes (/proc/self/root) were all denied as stated. Moving a task into another group held: the owner is fixed, the frozen claim requires the owner, and rescopes are checked live and replayed by the audit. Event payload schemas are closed, and treeHash is hex-only, so forged events could not inject git arguments or override seq or actor. Prototype-named evidence ids did not crash the audit. Pin forgery by a non-pinner is reported. In the closure, reused dispatches, wrong role, step or tree, the closer's own review, a no-go overridden by a later go, a fixed finding on the closing tree, a proof reused across findings, a fix proof whose base is not the reviewed tree, a battery not tied to its own run, a failing baseline (mutate refuses BASELINE_RED) and blank, null or text accounting are refused or reported as designed. Forged records with orchestrator or reviewer actors are the admitted L-GF-17 and L-GF-19 residual. The battery's choice of test command is admitted under L-GF-26. Neither is reported as a finding.

findings.summary: mv removes its source, but the hook judges only the destination (scripts/hooks/guard.js:118): backend-engineer's 'mv web/index.html <outside>', 'mv .eccode/security.json <outside>' and 'mv contracts/openapi.json <outside>' are all allowed and the files are gone, while 'rm' of each is denied (GF-OWN-2, GF-CONF-1 hook half, GF-FRZ-1). Reproduction: review-e2/repro/hook-shell.test.js (test E2-1)

Hard links are not modelled: 'ln' and 'cp -l' are judged on the link name only (scripts/hooks/guard.js:118 and :121), and lib/greenfield/permissions.js:22-39 resolves symlinks, not shared inodes. backend-engineer runs 'ln -f web/index.html app/main.py', then appends to app/main.py (allowed), which rewrites frontend's file; the same works for .eccode/security.json, and with 'cp -l contracts/openapi.json app/main.py' a file-tool Write of app/main.py is allowed and an in-place write changes the sealed contract. Reproduction: review-e2/repro/hook-shell.test.js (test E2-2)

A cd followed by ';' or a newline is dropped (scripts/hooks/guard.js:100), and pushd is not modelled (only 'cd', :111), so a '../' target is resolved against the original cwd (:437), lands outside the project and is allowed: 'cd app; echo x > ../web/index.html', 'cd app<newline>echo y >> ../web/index.html' and 'pushd app && echo z >> ../web/index.html' all overwrite frontend's file for backend-engineer, while the '&&' form is denied. Reproduction: review-e2/repro/hook-shell.test.js (test E2-3)

A subagent's git apply, git mv and git rm write the working tree but are not modelled (scripts/hooks/guard.js:138 covers only checkout and restore): backend-engineer patches web/index.html, moves it into app/, and removes the sealed contracts/openapi.json, each allowed. Reproduction: review-e2/repro/hook-shell.test.js (test E2-4)

GF-OWN-4 attribution lists changes with 'git diff --name-only' (lib/project.js:110, used at lib/greenfield/ownership-ops.js:208), which applies git's rename detection: a frontend file moved to a backend path and committed is reported under its new name only, so 'eccode-gf attribute' exits 0 ('every changed path ... is attributed') and the removal of web/index.html is never attributed, contrary to L-GF-24 (a write no completion lists is found by attribute). Combined with E2-1, a cross-group deletion is neither refused nor found. Reproduction: review-e2/repro/attribute-rename.test.js

A dispatch input that is a hard link to .eccode/events.jsonl (gitignored, same inode) is recorded as an input, because the GF-CLOSE-5 check is by path and symlink only (lib/greenfield/closure.js:107-109); the symlinked form is refused (D2-4). Reproduction: review-e2/repro/closure-paths.test.js (test E2-6)

The clean-tree check (lib/greenfield/closure.js:47) forces three git settings but still honours core.excludesFile and .git/info/exclude, which are repository configuration outside the reviewed tree: an untracked app/override.py imported by the committed app/main.py makes the tree dirty, but is reported clean once listed in either, contrary to D2-2's stated aim that repository git configuration cannot hide a change. Reproduction: review-e2/repro/closure-paths.test.js (test E2-7)

The managed-path preflight (lib/greenfield/preflight.js:45-46, :71) reads only the hook matcher and its own process environment: a sandbox install with an 'env' entry setting ECCODE_HOOKS=off (which the guard obeys, scripts/hooks/guard.js:369) or 'disableAllHooks' in .claude/settings.json or settings.local.json is still reported as regime managed-path with no warning. That the harness applies those settings to the hook process was not verified here. Reproduction: review-e2/repro/preflight-off.test.js

data.summary:
R3 READINESS, scope S2, dispatch disp-mw6rfuf7-0102fc00, tree bceec2cbe263030da0148c65c79bac2c0bb23b67 (HEAD 21ef6eb). Verdict: GO.

Question judged: is S2, as built in this tree, ready to be closed against what design sections 16, 17 and 18, the S2 plan and the limits register say S2 must deliver. The closure record's own conditions (batteries, resolutions, accounting) were left to the engine, as dispatched.

Reasons, each with its citation:

1. Frozen set untouched. The frozen v3 check prints "frozen: 48 files" (ev:ev-mw6ri2qa-01220de2). No S2 commit (3f6ee65..HEAD, 17 commits, 40 files) touches the 48 frozen files, the freeze file, docs/limits.md or scripts/guards (ev:ev-mw6rid22-01861160). No frozen file requires lib/greenfield or names eccode-gf, and the two edited engine files, lib/mcp.js and scripts/hooks/guard.js, are not frozen (ev:ev-mw6rvil6-01bc1538). A first, broader version of that check failed only because "greenfield" is also the frozen track name (ev-mw6rv94r-0113dfbd, superseded, not cited).

2. Tests pass. All 25 gf test files: 920 tests, 0 failures (ev:ev-mw6rjbpz-01c65c79). Full suite, npm run check with ECCODE_PYTHON at /root/.cache/eccode/phase3-venv: 1520 tests, 1506 pass, 0 fail, 14 skipped (ev:ev-mw6rpjk2-01e89d2e). The 14 skips are exactly the ones 16.8 item 1 names (docs/design/greenfield-senior.md:737): 6 Mealie checkout, 4 ECCODE_MEALIE_VALIDATE, 1 ECCODE_REALBUGS_VALIDATE, 1 ECCODE_CBM, 1 kotlinc, 1 codebase-memory-mcp. The FastAPI-dependent files run 70 tests with 0 skipped with the venv, against 30 skipped without it (ev:ev-mw6rtnox-0190fc75).

3. The rules of 16.2 exist and work. My own probe, separate from the authors' tests, runs the real hook as a child process and the lib/greenfield entry points: 52 of 52 checks pass (ev:ev-mw6rz4ql-0167b6ff). It covers GF-OWN-2: both halves (the group's globs, then the claimed task, scripts/hooks/guard.js:511 then scripts/hooks/guard.js:518), denyGlobs, an unowned path with its remedy (lib/greenfield/permissions.js:66), lexical normalisation, and a shell write. It covers GF-FRZ-1: a non-api role, api with no open request (lib/greenfield/permissions.js:61), and a contract that is not in the seal. Drafts namespacing. GF-CONF-1 in the hook, in pin and in drift (lib/greenfield/pin.js:56). GF-OWN-1 failing closed: on a tampered breakdown, and on an unreadable log (lib/greenfield/permissions.js:85), with the orchestrator unaffected. A plain ECCode project is unchanged. GF-OWN-3 refuses before the frozen call. GF-OWN-5: rescope, a non-reviewer, a ".." glob, disjointness, a valid amendment, and the hook then reading the effective map. The audit replays a forged amendment and a forged completion. The audit carries the L-GF-17 managed-path section (lib/greenfield/preflight.js:71). GF-OWN-4: the function, and eccode-gf attribute exiting non-zero. Refusals for GF-CLOSE-1, 3, 4 and 5. On the managed path the owner half of GF-OWN-3 rests on the frozen claim and complete checks (lib/tasks.js:137, lib/tasks.js:237), and the audit checks it at lib/greenfield/ownership-ops.js:241. The closure's round-3 rules are present: a no-go stands (lib/greenfield/closure.js:379); the closer's own review does not count (lib/greenfield/closure.js:384); a finding fixed on the closing tree blocks (lib/greenfield/closure.js:390); two batteries are required (lib/greenfield/closure.js:394); accounting is checked (lib/greenfield/closure.js:407); working-record inputs are refused (lib/greenfield/closure.js:86).

4. Section 18's survivor claims hold. I applied each mutant by hand in a scratch clone. The ruby mutant at scripts/hooks/guard.js:123 fails 3 tests (ev:ev-mw6s2lqa-013f1486). The rescope early return at lib/greenfield/ownership-ops.js:127 fails 1 test (ev:ev-mw6s3anz-015969e0). The dispatch inputs schema at lib/greenfield/events.js:83 fails 2 tests (ev:ev-mw6s3ng3-012b02e0).

5. S2 does not claim later slices. lib/greenfield has no GF-PRE, GF-UX or GF-TOOL rule and no S3 to S6 event, and the event list holds only the 15 S1 and S2 types (ev:ev-mw6s18uv-010ec3d1). This matches the 17.1 table, where only Upgrade 2 is built in S2 (docs/design/greenfield-senior.md:754).

6. Limits honestly registered. Every L-GF id cited in the design, the plan and the code is a row with a disposition; the rows naming S2 are L-GF-3, 4, 17 and 19 to 28 (ev:ev-mw6s1gqu-0108c269). I checked the rows against the code. L-GF-24 (docs/limits-greenfield.md:32): the audit has no attribution section, only lib/greenfield/audit.js:161 and its siblings. L-GF-26 (docs/limits-greenfield.md:34): a deferral's limit only has to be a non-empty string (lib/greenfield/closure.js:267). L-GF-28 (docs/limits-greenfield.md:36): the paired-run branch has no tree condition (lib/greenfield/closure.js:223).

Residuals. None of them breaks a promised S2 deliverable.
(a) GF-OWN-3 judges filesChanged on the lexical path (lib/greenfield/ownership-ops.js:170). The plan's Review Focus 3 lists "a symlinked directory" for T3 (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-07-greenfield-senior-s2.md:32), and T3 has no test for it. Measured: the hook refuses the write through app/link -> web (GF-OWN-2), and attribution reports the file where it lands (GF-OWN-4) (ev:ev-mw6s12fx-010d6c32). The design, which takes precedence (docs/design/greenfield-senior.md:893), does not promise symlink resolution for GF-OWN-3. I suggest adding a test or a sentence in L-GF-24.
(b) The items of 16.8 item 5 come after the close (docs/design/greenfield-senior.md:740, docs/design/greenfield-senior.md:741): docs/build/gf-s2-evidence.md, the estimate-versus-actual table, the scoring of P4 to P7 and the end snapshot. None is in the tree: docs/design/greenfield-senior.md:895 refers to the evidence file, the ledger row for S2 says pending (docs/build/compute-ledger.md:36), and the wording test tolerates the file's absence (tests/gf-docs.test.js:22, tests/gf-docs.test.js:33). They are still owed after the close.
(c) The hook allows a tool call when it hits an internal error outside policy(), unless ECCODE_STRICT=1 (scripts/hooks/guard.js:533). The fail-closed of GF-OWN-1 lives inside policy() (lib/greenfield/permissions.js:85). This is the hook's best-effort class (L-GF-1).

Not checked: the closure record's batteries, resolutions and accounting (left to the engine); the truth of the token figures; whether the earlier reviewers really had zero context (L-GF-19); the skip count of 49 before S2 (only the FastAPI files were compared with and without the venv).

data.summary:
S2 makes the group ownership declared in the sealed breakdown into enforced, path-scoped permissions, takes the shell away from group roles in favour of a runner, pins the guard configurations, and makes slice closure an engine rule.

Ownership map. It is not copied: it is the sealed breakdown.json's groups (globs, denyGlobs, roles), checked against the seal hashes on every read, plus reviewer amendments (gf.ownership.amended) applied in log order, each with `from` equal to the globs in force. Every map passes one shared check (disjoint; contracts/** and mocks/** api's, tests/acceptance/** test's) and a conservative algebra: two groups' globs may overlap only when one is provably inside the other and the outer group denies it; anything unprovable is refused. An amendment needs a design, verification or phase reviewer, a 30-character reason and a recorded message, changes globs only, and may not strand a pending or claimed task. A rescope may not leave its group.

Enforcement (P wrapped engine call, H hook, A audit replay). GF-OWN-1: owners in groups, open tasks inside effective globs (P at seal, A; after the seal H fails closed if the breakdown's hash or the policy cannot be checked). GF-OWN-2 (H): a group role's write must lie in its group's globs and a claimed task's; unowned paths and multi-link targets are refused. GF-OWN-3 (P, A): the completer is the task's owner and the listed files are in that group. GF-OWN-4: attribution, a function and a command; audit integration in S4. GF-FRZ-1 (H): contract files only by api, after the seal only under an open amendment request. Drafts are namespaced per group. A project is Greenfield-Senior when its record holds gf.project.initialized; an unreadable log fails closed.

Shell and runner. Shell-text judging kept being bypassed, so GF-RUN-1 denies group roles Bash, PowerShell and Monitor. GF-RUN-2's runner accepts plan-pinned commands or pinned forms of eight tools in a restricted word syntax, runs them through the frozen evidence runner (whose integrity window fails changes to the record or to tracked files outside the claim), and reports, without logging, new untracked files outside the group. A missing tool is "unverifiable here".

Guard-config pin. gf.config.pinned hashes behavior.json, guards.json and security.json with a label and a reason; the latest pin is the reference; group roles never write them; an orchestrator or user re-pin is recorded, not refused.

Closure. A scope closes only when, on a clean HEAD^{tree}, comprehension, critique and readiness each have a valid review from its own orchestrator-recorded dispatch (inputs hashed, working-record paths refused), by a reviewer role that authored nothing and is not the closer; readiness is go and no no-go stands on that tree; every finding is fixed (fix-verify, or a paired run for documentation), withdrawn by its raiser, or deferred by the user (minor, or major documentation); closing-tree findings cannot be fixed, so a fix forces a new round; at least two batteries exist, the first before any review and the last on the closing tree after the last fix, every survivor with a reason; accounting has a fixed form. Then nothing more is recorded for the scope.

Identity. The log asserts actors and does not bind them. Ownership between groups, and closure independence, hold only while the role-locked servers with the harness tool list and the hook hold. S2 adds a preflight that reports the regime (computed now, not logged), makes GF-OWN-3 check the plan's owner, and restates L-GF-17; keyed attestation is proposed only. A forger who names the owner passes; with hooks off nothing stops a spoof; content-addressed artifacts still catch changes outside their recorded change paths.

Accounting. All processed tokens (input, output, cache read, cache write) from the harness, snapshotted at slice and round boundaries; stale snapshots and resets give "unmeasurable"; GF-CLOSE-4 checks form only.

Not guaranteed: individual agents of a role and a fresh-context reviewer (L-GF-3, L-GF-19); drafts reads; authors' conclusions in the tree (L-GF-23); a closure surviving later commits (L-GF-27); a paired run's tree and relevance (L-GF-28, L-GF-30); untracked runner writes as events (L-GF-29); the truth of the accounting figures and deferral limit ids (L-GF-26); rescope message citations (L-GF-31); Semgrep, Gitleaks and Trivy runs here (L-GF-32).

findings.summary: 18.3 (closing paragraph) and 18.5 (L-GF-19 paragraph): closure independence over eccode-gf rests on 'the --actor argument does, which the hook checks as text', and 18.5 concludes 'the rule gives no way to record them as one'. No dispatched document states that check's condition: what --actor is compared with, and how a caller without an agent_type is treated. 18.3's last vector row lists 'the harness sends no agent_type' among the cases that 'nothing' stops, and the documents do not say whether the orchestrator's calls carry one. The only pointer, 'limits rows 91, 117', is in docs/limits.md, outside these documents. So a reader cannot tell whether the orchestrator, which keeps its shell (18.4), can record a closing review under a reviewer role through eccode-gf in the guard profile, where that shell can write the record.

18.3, last vector row: 'the hook is off (ECCODE_HOOKS=off in the process or in the project settings, disableAllHooks) or the harness sends no agent_type ... the preflight reports the hooks switched off (F0)'. F0 as stated reads only the project settings ('in .claude/settings.json or .claude/settings.local.json'). Nothing says the preflight detects ECCODE_HOOKS=off in an agent's process environment, hooks switched off in other settings files, or a harness that sends no agent_type. The row claims more than F0 is described as doing, and the residual for those cases is not stated.

18.6 says 'A counter reset ... the difference is then written unmeasurable, and both snapshots stay recorded as numbers'. GF-CLOSE-4 (18.5) requires 'end >= start when both are numbers', so a closure whose accounting keeps both reset-affected snapshots as numbers is refused. The documents do not say whether 'stay recorded as numbers' means the ledger only, nor what the closer writes into gf.slice.closed accounting{start, end} for a slice whose counter reset.

18.6 says 'Cost is the harness-reported cost_usd of the same call, a measurement', and its table shows $24.70 at S2 start and $18.96 for the S1 review phase. Against this stand 16.1 item 6, 'no paid runs, $0 on the meter', and 16.7, 'Paid runs | $0'. The documents do not say what cost_usd measures (a notional list-price figure or a charge), or how a non-zero measured cost squares with '$0 on the meter'. 18.6 reconciles cost only with D6's 'no dollar figures', which is about estimates.

18.4 and 17.5 disagree on the three scanners. 18.4 says 'Semgrep, Gitleaks and Trivy are not' installed here (L-GF-32 says the same). 17.5 lists them under 'Pinned (installed here)' (Gitleaks 8.30.1, Semgrep 1.184.0, Trivy 0.76.2), 'Measured in this sandbox', with Gitleaks re-run by the author. The runner's pinned forms in 18.4 also differ from 17.5's pinned invocations: 'gitleaks detect ... --report-format=json' against 'gitleaks dir or gitleaks git, with --no-banner --redact -f json -r <out> --exit-code 7', 'semgrep scan' against 'semgrep --config <pinned rule dir> ... --disable-version-check', and different trivy flags. Yet L-GF-32 says S4a 'installs and pins them'. Neither the environment difference nor which pin governs the runner is stated.

18.4: 'Every tool the owner listed has a pinned form, so none needs a blocking limit.' The owner's list is not reproduced in these documents, so the claim has no stated basis. The only tool list here, 17.5's six tools, includes T6 pre-commit, which has no runner form; the runner's eight tools are pytest, alembic, uvicorn, ruff, semgrep, gitleaks, trivy and playwright.

18.1 GF-OWN-1 says 'the seal-time half already exists as GF-WBS-1/2', and 18.2 says 'the same checks as GF-WBS-2 (groups disjoint; contracts/** and mocks/** belong to api, tests/acceptance/** to test)'. GF-WBS-2 is not in section 8's rule catalog, which lists only GF-WBS-1, with 'disjoint globs'; 18.5 assigns the check that roles agree with the constants to GF-WBS-1. No document states which checks belong to GF-WBS-1 and which to GF-WBS-2, so the rule id a refusal carries is unknown.

18.2's algebra says 'Overlapping globs of two groups are allowed only when one is provably inside the other and the outer group lists it in its denyGlobs'. As written, it refuses the default map in 2.4, the group table that S2's groups and roles come from: backend 'app/** excluding app/db/**' and security 'app/auth/**' overlap, and backend does not deny app/auth/**. The documents neither correct 2.4's defaults nor say that the algebra supersedes them. (2.4 was read because it sits next to 2.2 and defines the groups section 18 names.)

18.1 Clarifications: 'The G1 artifacts live under .eccode/artifacts/ (written by the document authors, delivery-lead included, ...) and under contracts/ (drafted by the document authors and the orchestrator before the seal)'. 'Document authors' is never defined. With delivery-lead among them, the sentence conflicts with GF-FRZ-1's 'a non-api group role is refused', because delivery-lead is a group role. Before the seal it is also unclear which rule decides an api-group write to contracts/: GF-FRZ-1 says api may write, while 'Before the seal, group roles hold no claim, so the hook's existing claimed-task rule answers'. A reader cannot tell who may write contracts/ before the seal.

18.1 GF-OWN-4: 'every path changed since a base commit is owned by a group that completed a task declaring it'. 'Declaring' is not defined: it could mean the task's planned files globs or the files its completion listed (L-GF-24's 'a write that no completion lists is found by eccode-gf attribute' suggests the latter). The base commit used in S2, before gf.slice.opened exists, is not stated either, including who supplies it to eccode-gf attribute.

Section 7 gives gf.slice.closed the fields 'steps{comprehension, critique, readiness}' and 'batteries[]'. 18.5 says 'every valid review of a step on the closing tree counts' and allows a step to be reviewed more than once. It does not say what steps{} holds (one review id per step, all of them, or nothing the engine relies on), which batteries batteries[] must list, or whether the engine reads these fields or recomputes them from the log.

18.5 'Clean tree' defines the check as 'git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all ...; untracked files that are not ignored count as dirty', with three git settings forced, but does not say which ignore rules apply. 18.7 (round 4) says 'the clean-tree check reads only the tree's own .gitignore files (E2-7)', so not .git/info/exclude or core.excludesFile, which plain git status honours. The paragraph that 18.5 presents as the definition leaves this out.

18.7, Closure row: 'As designed: one closing review (18.5)'. 18.5 is the as-built three-step rule. The pre-build single review is 16.5's text in commit 4799154 (16.5 now only points to 18.5), so the reference sends the reader to the wrong place.

18.3 says 'What a spoof does not buy: ... the sealed acceptance tests are content-addressed (GF-FRZ-2, GF-CONF-1, GF-ACC-2)', and L-GF-17 says the same. This sits in the as-built section, but GF-ACC-1/2 are registered for S3 (17.7, L-GF-7). The text does not say that this protection is not yet built in S2, so a reader takes it as in force now.

Two statements still describe group-role shell writes, which GF-RUN-1 (18.4) removed in a Greenfield-Senior project: section 2.2 ('a shell write (group roles have a shell in the sandbox and guard profiles) is judged on its command text only') and L-GF-24, an S2 limit ('In S2 ... a shell write is judged on its command text, L-GF-1'). Section 18's precedence clause settles what is built. But the register's statement of S2's residual for cross-group writes is stale: it leaves out GF-RUN-1 and the runner path (L-GF-29).

data.summary:
R2 CRITIQUE (hostile review), scope S2, security-reviewer. Focus: the diff 21ef6eb..HEAD and the
shell-class closure (GF-RUN-1 no shell for a group role; GF-RUN-2 the runner).

WHAT I ATTACKED

GF-RUN-1 (no shell for a group role). I drove scripts/hooks/guard.js with every group role in
C.GROUPS (integration-engineer, backend-engineer, database-engineer, security-engineer,
frontend-engineer, test-engineer, delivery-lead, devops-engineer) against Bash, PowerShell and
Monitor. All are denied with the GF-RUN-1 reason; the orchestrator, reviewer roles, roles in no
group, and group roles outside a Greenfield-Senior project keep their shell; a Greenfield-Senior
record whose log cannot be parsed fails closed (denied). The matcher wiring in hooks/hooks.json and
lib/install.js now carries Bash|PowerShell|Monitor, and preflight.matcherWired requires all three.
permissions.shellDenial fails closed on an exception and returns null only for the orchestrator or a
non-group role. The denial is placed before the rest of guard.js main() and exits immediately. I
could not find a group role that keeps a shell inside a sealed project, nor a tool-name gap among the
three the design names. roleOf cannot be set by the agent (L-GF-17 control, admitted). This held.

GF-RUN-2 (the runner). I attacked the command grammar (words()/parse()): shell metacharacters,
redirections, command substitution, pipes, backquotes, tabs/newlines, `-p`/`-o`/`--rootdir` pytest
flags, `python -c`, `bash -c`, `node`, out-of-project and absolute path args, `alembic revision`
outside migrations/, semgrep without --metrics=off, gitleaks without --redact, serve with a non-check
inner form, writing forms by a non-owning group, `ruff format` with no paths and with `.`. Every one
is refused. The serve form builds a child command out of WORD-validated tokens and quotes execPath and
the script path; ECCODE_GF_PYTHON is WORD-validated; I found no injection. Forging events via project
code is stopped by the frozen record window (events.jsonl/state.json/config.json snapshot+restore).
New untracked files outside the caller's group are reported.

WHAT BROKE

F2-1 (major, engine behavior). 18.3's spoof matrix row "A runs project code through the runner, and
the code writes B's files" names its stop as "the frozen integrity window fails a run that changes a
tracked file outside A's claimed ownership", and L-GF-29 repeats that positive claim. It is not met
for a tracked file that belongs to ANOTHER group's CURRENTLY-CLAIMED task. The frozen
changedOutsideOwnership (lib/evidence.js) splits such changes into `outside` (owned by no claimant,
which fails the run, exit 99) and `concurrent` (matches another agent's claimed globs, which is only
RECORDED, not failed). runner.js adds an untracked-file check but no tracked-concurrent check, so a
group role whose pytest/conftest/app code modifies another group's claimed tracked file gets
status=passed, ok=true, problems=[]. Reproduced in concurrent.test.js: backend-engineer (claims
s0-app) runs `pytest -q app/test_cross.py`, whose test appends to web/index.html (frontend's claimed
s0-web, web/**); the run is recorded passed with integrity=null and only a buried concurrent:
["web/index.html"] field the runner never surfaces. The write is still visible in git and
attributable by GF-OWN-4, so this weakens rather than nullifies the control: major, not blocking.

F2-2 (minor, engine behavior). 18.4 enumerates the runner's plan-pinned commands as "task checks, the
behaviour command, the detected stack checks". runner.formProblems' first line short-circuits on
mcp.approvedCommands, which also returns s.lab.repro.command. A command equal to the pinned
reproduction bypasses every form check (even `bash -c ...`). lab_repro over MCP requires an
already-approved command, but `eccode debug repro --replace` lets the orchestrator or user pin an
arbitrary reproduction, which a group role can then run verbatim through gf_run. The integrity window
still applies, so impact is bounded; the finding is that the accepted-command set is broader than 18.4
states. Reproduced in labrepro.probe.js.

WHAT ELSE HELD. The clean-tree E2-7 change (status -uno plus ls-files --others
--exclude-per-directory=.gitignore) is stricter, not weaker: a malicious .git/info/exclude or global
excludesFile no longer hides an untracked file, and a modified tracked .gitignore still shows as dirty
under -uno. The E2-6 hard-link dispatch-input check and the E2-5 changedSince (both rename names,
--no-renames, base option-injection guard) are sound. The preflight E2-8 reads disableAllHooks /
env.ECCODE_HOOKS=off from settings.json and settings.local.json. The GF-CLOSE-2 round-5 change allows
the user to defer only a minor finding or a major documentation finding; a major defect, a blocking
finding and a non-user deferral are refused, and a forged deferral is flagged by the audit. The tree's
own gf-runner (52), gf-review-s2-e2 and gf-review suites pass.

findings.summary: [engine behavior] The runner's integrity window does NOT fail a run that writes another group's concurrently-claimed tracked file, contradicting 18.3's spoof-matrix 'Stopped by' and L-GF-29 ('fails a run that changes ... a tracked file outside the caller's claimed ownership'). lib/greenfield/runner.js run() relies on the frozen lib/evidence.js changedOutsideOwnership, which classifies a changed tracked file in another agent's claimed globs as 'concurrent' (recorded only), not 'outside' (fails, exit 99); runner.js adds an untracked-file check but no tracked-concurrent check. Reproduced in review-f2/concurrent.test.js: backend-engineer (claims s0-app) runs 'pytest -q app/test_cross.py' whose test appends to web/index.html (frontend's claimed s0-web); the run records status=passed, ok=true, problems=[], integrity=null, only a buried concurrent:['web/index.html']. Visible in git and attributable by GF-OWN-4, so it weakens rather than nullifies the stated stop.

[engine behavior] The runner's plan-pinned-command bypass accepts a source 18.4 does not enumerate ('task checks, the behaviour command, the detected stack checks'). runner.js formProblems' first line short-circuits on mcp.approvedCommands, which also returns s.lab.repro.command (lib/mcp.js:236); a command equal to the pinned reproduction bypasses every pinned-form check, including shell syntax like 'bash -c ...'. lab_repro over MCP requires an already-approved command, but 'eccode debug repro --replace' (lib/lab.js recordRepro, no requireApproved on the replace path) lets the orchestrator/user pin an arbitrary reproduction a group role can then run verbatim through gf_run; the integrity window still applies, so impact is bounded. Reproduced in review-f2/labrepro.probe.js.

data.summary:
R3 READINESS, scope S2, tree 154055e2498bc8b034116d7bb786c29f9dd000be (commit c79800b). Verdict: NO-GO.

The question was whether S2 as built delivers what section 18 says it builds. Most of it does. One rule that section 18 promises, GF-RUN-2's restriction on the writing forms, is broken in a way that lets one group rewrite another group's files on the managed path. The brief says that is a NO-GO.

Reason 1 (decisive): the writing forms of the runner accept a directory that holds another group's files. Design 18.4 says `ruff check --fix` and `ruff format` take "at least one path, each inside the caller's group" and write "the named paths" (docs/design/greenfield-senior.md:881). The check judges each argument with ownerOfPath (lib/greenfield/runner.js:147). ownerOfPath matches the argument as if it were a file (lib/greenfield/ownership.js:73). So the directory name `app/db` matches backend's `app/**` and does not match db's deny glob `app/db/**`. My probe on the sample map: backend-engineer is accepted for `ruff format app/db`, `ruff format app/auth`, `ruff check --fix app/db` and `ruff format app/`, with no problem reported. The controls `ruff format app` and `ruff format web` are refused (ev:ev-mw6yr1kj-01ca3854, status failed, as a no-go may cite).

End to end, with db holding its claim on s0-db (the normal state in a parallel phase), backend-engineer's `ruff format app/db` rewrote db's tracked app/db/models.py. The run passed with exit 0, the runner reported no problem, and the frozen evidence named the file only as `concurrent` (ev:ev-mw6yrahc-01f12021; lib/evidence.js:234). With no db claim, the frozen integrity window failed the same run with exit 99, but only after the write had happened (same evidence). GF-RUN-1 makes the runner a group role's only way to run a command, and S2 exists to refuse cross-group writes. Here the runner's own pinned form makes such a write and nothing flags it.

Reason 2: the limit for that backstop is not registered accurately. L-GF-29 (docs/limits-greenfield.md:37) and 18.3's vector row (docs/design/greenfield-senior.md:859) say the frozen window fails a run that changes a tracked file outside the caller's claimed ownership. The frozen window passes such a change when another active claim owns the file. The main register says so (docs/limits.md:131, row 88; lib/evidence.js:234), but the greenfield register does not. Demonstrated: a pytest test run by backend-engineer changed frontend's claimed web/index.html, and the run passed with no runner problem (ev:ev-mw6yrahc-01f12021, fourth test). In a parallel phase, the containment that L-GF-29 states does not hold.

Reason 3 (minor): 18.4 says alembic is installed here (docs/design/greenfield-senior.md:887). On this machine alembic is only in the venv, not on PATH, so the pinned alembic form runs as "unverifiable here" (ev:ev-mw6yrahc-01f12021, third test). L-GF-32 names only Semgrep, Gitleaks and Trivy (docs/limits-greenfield.md:40). The runner's fail-closed behaviour is correct; the registration is incomplete. L-GF-24 still says a shell write is judged on its command text (docs/limits-greenfield.md:32), which GF-RUN-1 replaced for group roles.

What is delivered and works:
- GF-RUN-1 is built in scripts/hooks/guard.js:388 and lib/greenfield/permissions.js:97, and is described at docs/design/greenfield-senior.md:823. Every group role is denied Bash, PowerShell and Monitor. An unreadable log fails closed. Orchestrator and reviewer roles keep their shell. The install wires the guard for all three tools (lib/install.js:68), and the preflight requires that wiring (lib/greenfield/preflight.js:17).
- GF-RUN-2 is described at docs/design/greenfield-senior.md:824 and exposed as gf_run (lib/greenfield/index.js:75). It has pinned forms for all eight tools and refuses shell syntax. Runs go through the frozen evidence runner. The uvicorn serve form starts the app, runs the check and stops the server. A tool that is missing reports "unverifiable here". tests/gf-runner.test.js: 52 tests pass, 0 skipped (ev:ev-mw6yewxy-01dcb686).
- Full suite with ECCODE_PYTHON pointing at the venv: 1,600 tests, 1,586 pass, 0 fail, 14 skipped. The 14 are exactly those named in 16.8 (docs/design/greenfield-senior.md:652): 6 need a Mealie checkout, 4 need ECCODE_MEALIE_VALIDATE, 1 REALBUGS, 1 CBM, 1 kotlinc, 1 codebase-memory-mcp (ev:ev-mw6ykdj5-012fdc0d).
- The frozen set checks as 48 files (ev:ev-mw6yelal-01bd9a11). No frozen file, docs/limits.md or scripts/guards/*.py has changed since the S1 end commit 3f6ee65 (ev:ev-mw6yramh-0180c996).
- S2 claims no item of S3 to S6 as built.

Not checked: real Semgrep, Gitleaks and Trivy runs (they are not installed); a Playwright run end to end (only its form was checked); gf_run over a live MCP stdio session; the harness's own agent_type and Monitor behaviour beyond the hook's simulated input; the closure record's own conditions (the engine's to check).
